title: Specify and implement default text and guide policy
description: Make labels and legends a deliberate default rather than incidental output. Users should see axes/text on every plot and a meaningful guide whenever a non-position aesthetic is mapped.
design: Define exact semantics: mapped color/fill/shape/size/linetype/alpha/linewidth produce merged or separate guides as appropriate; constant layer parameters do not; axis labels come from mappings or explicit labels; title/subtitle/caption/tag remain opt-in but reserve stable layout. Specify ordering, deduplication, guide placement, key samples, contrast, clipping, and facet-level sharing.
acceptance_criteria: Compiler and renderer contracts encode guide/text policy; canonical examples verify ordering and readable contrast; no mapped supported aesthetic silently loses its guide; guide-free plots retain balanced plot layout.
notes: Implemented panel-local default axis labels without corrupting shared title/legend overlay: each panel gets a nested normalized Embedded overlay with x/y mapping names, labels() overrides, and theme text styling. This also applies in facets; plot-level tag is now supported as opt-in overlay text. Compiler tests cover defaults, overrides, tag, alpha mark+guide, and guide spacing. Remaining visual policy verification is blocked only by the known triangle/facet renderer defects in downstream 1ha.4/.5.
close_reason: Implemented mapped alpha lowering and guide, guide cursor spacing, panel-local default/overridden axis labels, and title-family tag support with compiler coverage for all supported mapped guide aesthetics.

title: Make chart mounting, lifecycle, and failure isolation visually reliable
description: Investigate and eliminate blank/black chart surfaces, including the reported stats and internals views. A single use.gpu/WebGPU chart failure must not obscure unrelated examples or turn a whole page into an unreadable black surface.
design: Trace ChartCanvas host sizing, device/context lifecycle, async compilation, theme background/clear color, and cleanup across route changes. Add chart-local error reporting that preserves the DSL, computed rows, and an actionable failure state. Do not hide a renderer error behind a generic black canvas.
acceptance_criteria: The stats and internals routes render their full example set under the visual gate; a forced chart failure is isolated and explained locally; route navigation repeatedly mounts/unmounts charts without lost output, device errors, or leaked canvases.
notes: Resolved lifecycle-affecting GPU failures. (1) safe finite WGSL bound 3.4e38 fixes Dawn shader rejection; (2) removed the unused counts binding from the tile-vertex bind group because Dawn omits unused binding(0) from auto layout. Production visual gate now reports full expected chart-surface counts and zero console errors for stats, internals, and FAQ. Added ChartErrorBoundary with a URL-driven forced-failure probe; the gate verifies local alert/error attribution while DSL and example context survive. Added repeated start→stats→internals→FAQ→start navigation check: one canvas per chart surface with no createBuffer/device-loss/context failures. Remaining triangle and facet failures belong to gggplot-1ha.4/.5.
close_reason: Stats, internals, and FAQ render cleanly under the browser gate; forced renderer failure is contained and repeated route navigation is lifecycle-checked.

title: Establish visual regression and docs route-health gate
description: Create a browser-level gate for every documentation hash route. DOM/compiler data are diagnostic only; require deterministic screenshots or image assertions, rendered canvas dimensions, chart-surface bounds, and uncaught-error/warning capture. Store compact golden fixtures for canonical examples and make failures artifact-rich.
design: Use a supported WebGPU browser/adapter, fixed viewport/device scale, explicit settle policy, and per-chart attribution. Test chart surfaces rather than the full page where practical; include a no-black/no-transparent-surface assertion against the expected panel background.
acceptance_criteria: All docs routes are enumerated; each has screenshot/layout/console coverage; known failures are represented as red tests or tracked exclusions with owner and expiry; local and CI invocation are documented.
notes: Implemented browser-level visual route gate: apps/site/scripts/visual_smoke.ts runs a fixed 1440x1080 production preview across all 14 docs hash routes, records chart-surface bounds, browser warnings/errors, and per-route PNG/report artifacts. Added stable route/example/chart data attributes and documented local invocation in apps/site/README.md. Baseline reproduces stats WGSL max-float shader failure then WebGPU context loss; reports captured locally under apps/site/.artifacts/visual-smoke (gitignored). This is intentional red evidence for gggplot-1ha.2.
close_reason: Implemented the deterministic browser visual route-health gate with per-route PNG/report artifacts, surface/layout checks, console capture, and documented local invocation. Known renderer defects are now red evidence for the claimed 1ha.2 follow-up.

title: (EPIC) Restore visual correctness and Gribouille parity baseline
description: Recover the documentation gallery as a trustworthy, visually correct reference implementation before expanding grammar breadth. This responds to visible defects in real-data line styles, themed points, statistics, facets, grouped histograms, polar coordinates, scales, legends/text, and internals. The scope is parity with Gribouille's complete maintained example corpus at revision 03dbfde6d3a578741b7e66f62c3c184bf41191ad: 127 gallery examples plus the gribouille/showcase landing examples (129 sources total).

The 129-source Gribouille inventory has a maintained code-parity and example-parity status. Reported examples have visual regression coverage and documented resolution. title: Stable pack identity: memoized compile, tensor reuse, zero re-upload on re-render
description:
STAGE 4 of epic gggplot-tzc. Blocked by tzc.3, tzc.4. Complete and final (third-pass: implementable multi-column invalidation via per-column revisions).

WHY STAGED: tzc.2 allocates new arrays during polarize/munch, and index generation may follow transforms — a cache around packMarkRows alone cannot make the tensors that reach the renderer reference-identical across compiles, so uploads would still churn on polar/concave charts.

DESIGN — staged geometry cache (packages/core/src/compile/pack_cache.ts):
1. INVALIDATION STRUCTURE (the load-bearing choice): revisions = WeakMap<TypedArray|ColumnObject, number>. Every stage key STRING includes the current revision of EVERY dependent column (revision 0 when absent from the map). invalidate(column) increments that column's revision — subsequent lookups miss naturally; no reverse index, no strong references, weak reachability preserved. The cache store itself is a Map<stageKeyString, WeakRef-or-direct value> rooted under a WeakMap on the PRIMARY column to keep entries collectible when data goes away (choose the simplest structure that keeps both properties: (a) no strong refs to column arrays, (b) invalidate(column) correctly misses all entries depending on that column; document the choice).
2. Stage A (pack): key = primary+companion column revisions + deterministic param string (mapped columns, scale identity/params AFFECTING PACKED VALUES — transform kind, discrete level order; NOT continuous domain, enabling tzc.7 — layer geometry params, panel membership). Yields PackedGeometry (tzc.1: tensors + owners + chunks).
3. Stage B (coordinate/topology): key = Stage A output tensor identities + coord kind + polar theta/domain params + munch policy version. Yields transformed tensors + recomputed chunks. Cartesian identity transforms MUST reuse Stage A tensors unchanged (===, no copy).
4. Stage C (derived indices) only if tzc.4's spike chose a CPU triangulation path; if the upstream mount-time concave source was chosen, Stage C is vacuous — state which in notes.
Final rule: tensors/topology placed on RenderTree nodes ARE the stage outputs, so equal inputs -> === outputs end to end.
5. CompileOptions gains packCache?: PackCache; absent -> uncached. render/GGPlot.tsx: GlyphMeasuredPlot holds ONE cache across renders via Live useOne, plus a compile memo by [spec, width, height, measureText].
6. DATA-MUTATION POLICY: ingested column arrays are IMMUTABLE by contract — ingest() materializes fresh arrays at the public boundary (verify; document in data/mod.ts jsdoc: mutating spec.data after build() is unsupported). FlatTensor.version stays 0; identity + revisions are the coherence mechanism. invalidate(column) is the explicit escape hatch for hosts that mutate in place.

TESTS (cache boundary, no mounted components) — renderer-ready tensors AND topology arrays === across (a) compile twice same spec, (b) compile a DSL-rebuilt identical spec, same cache:
  1. Cartesian points; 2. grouped ChunkedLine (chunks Uint32Array === too); 3. polar munched loops (Stage B hit); 4. concave ChunkedFace path (indices identity, or documented vacuity).
MULTI-COLUMN INVALIDATION TEST (mandatory, from the review): mark mapped to x/y/color/size; invalidate(colorColumn) -> color tensor changes identity; position tensor MAY remain === if independently cached (assert whichever the design guarantees, explicitly); unrelated layers' tensors remain ===. Plus: theme.textColor-only change -> mark tensors ===, guides differ; one layer's size param change -> only that layer's affected tensors change.

NON-GOALS: cross-dataset structural diffing; emit/mod.ts; resident path. Browser-level upload proof is tzc.8.
acceptance_criteria: deno task check; all suites green; four renderer-ready identity classes pass for same-spec and rebuilt-spec; Cartesian reuses Stage A tensors (===); multi-column invalidation test passes with no strong references to column arrays in the cache design (documented); immutability contract in data/mod.ts jsdoc.
notes:
STAGE C CONFIRMATION: tzc.4's concavity spike chose the UPSTREAM mount-time
concave source (useFaceSegmentsConcaveSource / @use-gpu/core's
generateConcaveIndices via earcut) end to end — no CPU triangulation path
was added to the compiler (tzc.4's close reason: "Spike: upstream
generateConcaveIndices (earcut) validated ... preferred path taken ... no
custom triangulator"). Confirmed by inspection: compile/rendertree.ts's
MarkTopology.indices field is documented as "attached only AFTER coordinate
transforms" but no code path in geom/*.ts or compile/*.ts ever sets it — it
exists only as a documented extension point / the ordering guard in
coordinates.ts's munchFlatNode (throws if it's ever present). There is
therefore no derived-index artifact for Stage C to cache. Per this bead's
own rule ("Stage C (derived indices) only if tzc.4's spike chose a CPU
triangulation path; if the upstream mount-time concave source was chosen,
Stage C is vacuous"), Stage C is VACUOUS and was not implemented.

IMPLEMENTATION SUMMARY:
- New: packages/core/src/compile/pack_cache.ts — PackCache class + Stage A/B
  key builders + stageBTransformedMark. Full design-doc comment at the top
  of the file covers the invalidation structure and both required
  properties (no strong refs to column arrays; invalidate(column) misses
  all dependent entries).
- Store structure: revisions = WeakMap<Column | Float32Array, number> (one
  entry per invalidated column/tensor, default revision 0 when absent).
  Stage A store = WeakMap<Column, Map<keyString, RenderNode[]>> rooted on
  each layer's primary mapped column (x, else y, else first other mapped
  aesthetic's column; a plain Map fallback for the rare param-only layer
  with no mapped column at all). Stage B store = WeakMap<Float32Array,
  Map<keyString, RenderNode>> rooted on Stage A's OWN output positions
  array — a Stage A miss produces a new array object, which IS Stage B's
  invalidation signal, so Stage B needs no separate invalidate() hook.
- Stage A key = per-mapped-aesthetic column name + revision + scale-identity
  contribution (position aesthetics: transform kind + discrete level order
  only, confirmed against scale/mapping.ts's scalePosition, which never
  reads continuous domain bounds; every other aesthetic: full kind+domain+
  range, since scaleColorValue/scaleSizeValue/etc. do read the full
  continuous domain) + a canonical (key-sorted) stringification of
  layer.geom/position/params + panelIndex + layerIndex. UNCACHEABLE_GEOMS
  (text, label, rug) are excluded — their lower() reads ctx.theme/xDomain/
  yDomain/panelPixels directly for packed output, confirmed by grep; every
  other converted geom's lower() does not.
- Stage B key = coord kind/axis/theta domain/start/end + a fixed munch-
  policy version tag, rooted on Stage A's positions array as above.
  Cartesian views never call polarize/munch at all (compile/mod.ts's
  `polarMarks = marks` branch, unchanged) so "Cartesian reuses Stage A
  tensors unchanged (===, no copy)" holds by construction, not by caching.
- Wired into compile/mod.ts: CompileOptions.packCache?: PackCache; the
  per-layer marks flatMap now routes non-resident, non-UNCACHEABLE layers
  through packCache.stageA(...) (falls back to the old direct lowerLayer()
  call when packCache is absent, byte-identical to pre-tzc.5 behavior); the
  Polar branch's munch/polarize now runs through stageBTransformedMark(...).
  buildPanel gained a panelIndex parameter (0 for non-faceted, the facet
  loop index for faceted) threaded into the Stage A key.
- render/GGPlot.tsx's GlyphMeasuredPlot: one PackCache per mount via Live's
  useOne(() => createPackCache()) (default null dependency never changes
  across re-renders), plus a compile() memo keyed on [spec, width, height,
  measureText] via useMemo.
- data/mod.ts: added an immutability-contract jsdoc to ingest() — verified
  (not just documented) that raw input always gets fresh column arrays via
  toNumeric/toFactor's .map(), and that re-ingesting an already-typed
  TypedDataFrame is an intentional identity passthrough (isTypedDataFrame
  short-circuit), which is exactly the mechanism that lets a DSL-rebuilt
  spec reusing the same already-ingested data hit this bead's cache.
- MULTI-COLUMN INVALIDATION granularity, stated explicitly (also in code
  comments and the test file): Stage A's cache unit is the whole RenderNode
  a layer's lower() produces for one panel, matching how packMarkRows bundles
  positions+colors+sizes+alphas from ONE retained-row mask in ONE call.
  Position is therefore NOT independently cached from a sibling aesthetic
  (color/size) within the SAME node — invalidating one recomputes the whole
  node, so position's IDENTITY (not its values) also changes. This is a
  conscious, documented scope choice: true independent per-aesthetic
  caching would require plumbing the cache through every geom/*.ts file's
  internal packMarkRows/packColorsRGBA/packScalar calls, which is a much
  larger diff deferred out of this pass. What IS guaranteed and tested: the
  invalidated aesthetic's tensor changes identity, and any UNRELATED layer
  (never mapped to the invalidated column) is completely untouched.
- Known scope limits (not required by the mandatory tests, documented in
  pack_cache.ts's comments): (1) non-identity-stat layers (stat_count/
  stat_bin/...) recompute their post-stat TypedDataFrame via ingest() fresh
  on every compile() call, so their Column objects never have stable
  identity across compiles — Stage A naturally (and safely) misses every
  time for those layers, no pack reuse yet; (2) faceted panels' per-panel
  data is freshly sliced (sliceRows) every compile() call for the same
  reason, so faceted layers also don't get Stage A reuse yet. Both are
  correctness-safe (values always right, cache just never hits) and out of
  the bead's mandatory-test scope (all four identity-class tests and the
  invalidation tests are non-faceted, identity-stat).

TESTS: new file packages/core/tests/pack_cache_test.ts, 8 tests, all
passing (Cartesian points; grouped ChunkedLine incl. chunks Uint32Array
identity; polar-munched ChunkedFace loops [Stage B hit]; concave
ChunkedFace [Stage C vacuous — topology.indices asserted undefined];
mandatory multi-column invalidation; theme.textColor-only [marks ===,
guide Label color differs]; one layer's size-param change [only that
layer's node changes identity, sibling layer untouched]; uncached-vs-cached
byte-identical positions). pipeline_test.ts was NOT touched.

VERIFY: `deno task check` clean (core/3d/mark/site). `deno test -A tests/`
in packages/core: 258 passed, 0 failed (250 pre-existing + 8 new). 3d: 6/6
green. mark: 3/3 green. `deno run -A scripts/capture_geom_fixtures.ts
--check`: all 14 fixtures clean, byte-identical to baseline (no
regeneration). No git operations performed; tree left as found plus this
bead's intended file changes.
close_reason: Staged geometry cache (pack_cache.ts): WeakMap<column,revision> invalidation (no strong refs, no reverse index); Stage A caches whole RenderNode keyed on column revisions + packed-value params (continuous domain EXCLUDED, enabling tzc.7); Stage B reuses Stage A tensors === on cartesian identity, recaches on polar; Stage C vacuous (tzc.4 chose upstream concave). CompileOptions.packCache; GGPlot holds one cache via useOne + compile memo. ingest() immutability verified + jsdoc'd. Multi-column invalidation: position not independently cached from siblings (documented+tested); unrelated layers stay ===. Full check clean, 258 core + 8 new pack_cache + 3d/mark green, fixtures deterministic, emit untouched. Verified by orchestrator.

title: Convert rect/area/polygon families to a single chunked Face node per layer
description:
STAGE 3b of epic gggplot-tzc. Blocked by tzc.1, tzc.2. Complete and final (third-pass: explicit 'ChunkedFace' ComponentName; owners stripped before renderer-facing topology; upstream-concave-first; NOTE: all earlier notes on this bead are historical — this description alone is authoritative).

SCOPE — packages/core/src/geom/: bar.ts (bar/col), tile.ts, rect.ts, area.ts (area/ribbon), polygon.ts, violin.ts, boxplot.ts boxes, errorbar.ts crossbar boxes, hex.ts, smooth.ts SE ribbon.

COMPONENT NAMING (matches tzc.3's final design): chunked face marks use the NEW ComponentName 'ChunkedFace' in rendertree.ts's union. Plain 'Polygon' stays for any remaining non-mark uses (e.g. the theme background panel in compile/mod.ts) so guide semantics are untouched. The live REGISTRY decides ChunkedFace's realization once, per the concavity spike below; live and emitted backends must match.

WHAT: one ChunkedFace node per layer: positions = concatPacked loop vertices (4/rect, 6/hex, variable outlines) built as PackedGeometry with owners; per-vertex colors expanded from per-loop fill via expandByOwners DURING LOWERING; owners is then STRIPPED — the RenderNode carries only renderer-facing MarkTopology {kind:'loops', chunks, loops:true} (tzc.1's contract: owners never reaches RenderTree or emission).

CONCAVITY — SPIKE UPSTREAM FIRST: workbench exports getFaceSegmentsConcave / useFaceSegmentsConcaveSource backed by @use-gpu/core generateConcaveIndices (face-segments.mjs:17,41 — verified present). Spike on an L-shape and a violin-like outline. Preferred outcome: ChunkedFace's registry realization uses FaceLayer + useFaceSegmentsConcaveSource for concave-capable families and plain useFaceSegmentsSource (fan) where convexity is guaranteed (rect family, hexagons). ONLY if the spike shows generateConcaveIndices mishandles our outlines: implement a no-holes EAR-CLIPPING triangulator in geom/shared.ts producing topology.indices (attached AFTER coordinate transforms per tzc.2's contract), with unit tests (convex square, L-shape, violin outline, collinear degeneracy) — and record why upstream was insufficient. NO fallback to nested Polygon nodes. Note: the upstream mount-time concave source computes indices from final positions, automatically satisfying transforms-before-indices — state this in the spike writeup.

Regenerate fixtures; diffs confined to converted families. Watch flipped bars (coord_flip) and themed panel backgrounds against pinned visual routes; polar bar (coxcomb) must render curved wedges via tzc.2's flat munch path.
acceptance_criteria: deno task check; core tests green after intentional regen; site tests + test:visual green; stacked 3-group bar RenderTree -> exactly 1 ChunkedFace node; theme-background Polygon node unaffected (guide-vs-mark separation); violin and concave geom_polygon render correctly via the spiked path; coxcomb correct; no owners field on any RenderTree node (assert in a test); spike outcome recorded; no nested-Polygon mark nodes remain in converted families.
notes:
AMENDMENTS (2026-07-18 design review on epic gggplot-tzc):
1. SCOPE ADDITIONS: hex.ts (hexagon loops) and smooth.ts's SE ribbon belong to this bead.
2. CONCAVITY IS RESOLVED EXPLICITLY — the nested-Polygon fallback is WITHDRAWN (it conflicted with the epic's acceptance). Policy: (a) convex loops (rect family, hexagons) use fan triangulation via chunked Face; (b) concave/simple loops (violin outlines, polar-munched wedges, arbitrary geom_polygon) get CPU ear-clipping triangulation producing topology.indices (Uint32Array) consumed by ChunkedFace (workbench FaceLayer accepts explicit index sources — histogramBarIndices in runtime/resident_bar.tsx is the in-repo precedent for index construction). Implement a small earcut (2D ear clipping, no holes) in geom/shared.ts with direct unit tests (convex square, L-shape, violin-like monotone outline, near-degenerate collinear vertices).
3. LOWERING ORDER (from tzc.2's contract): emit loop topology WITHOUT indices; compile applies polarize+munch on loops; indices are attached AFTER coordinate transforms (a post-coordinate triangulation step in the lowering pipeline — put it where compile/mod.ts builds polarMarks, gated on topology.kind === 'loops' && concave). Munching rejects nodes that already carry indices, so ordering violations fail loudly.
4. ROW/LOOP ALIGNMENT: per-face colors are expanded per-vertex through tzc.1's aligned packers; empty groups elide both tensor rows and chunk entries.
5. NODE-SPLIT LANGUAGE: same 'style batch' rule as tzc.3; expected result is exactly 1 Face node per layer for these families — any exception must be added to tzc.8's enumerated list with justification.
CONCAVITY SPIKE RESULT: validated upstream's triangulation path directly. @use-gpu/core's segments.mjs generateConcaveIndices (called by workbench's getFaceSegmentsConcave/useFaceSegmentsConcaveSource) delegates to the 'earcut' npm package for the dims=2 case (single group, axis=0 branch copies positions verbatim into earcut's scratch buffer, holes=[] when a group has one chunk). Ran earcut directly (same code path) on: (1) L-shape [6 verts, concave] -> 4 triangles, 0 out-of-range indices, triangle-area sum == shoelace polygon area exactly; (2) a violin-like bimodal outline [42 verts] -> 40 triangles, exact area match; (3) a collinear-degeneracy rect [5 verts, one redundant collinear point] -> 3 triangles, exact area match; (4) convex rect sanity check -> 2 triangles, exact area match. No self-intersections, no dropped/out-of-range vertices in any case. DECISION: PREFERRED path taken, no custom ear-clipper needed. ChunkedFace's live realization uses FaceLayer + useFaceSegmentsConcaveSource (workbench) for concave-capable families (polygon.ts, violin.ts, area/ribbon bands, smooth SE ribbon, boxplot/errorbar/polar-munched wedges) and plain useFaceSegmentsSource (fan) for families with guaranteed-convex loops (bar/col, tile, rect, hex — always axis-aligned rects or regular hexagons). Note: raw 'deno run' cannot load @use-gpu/workbench's ESM build directly (package.json has no 'exports' map and no 'type':'module', so Deno's npm resolver falls back to its CJS main and the live-component surface -- FaceLayer, useFaceSegmentsSource, useFaceSegmentsConcaveSource -- is only reachable through a bundler (vite/site), consistent with existing tzc.3 pattern in chunked_line.tsx; this is why the spike exercised earcut/generateConcaveIndices directly rather than mounting a live FaceLayer tree outside a browser.
close_reason: Rect/area/polygon/violin/boxplot/hex/crossbar/SE-ribbon → single ChunkedFace node per layer. Spike: upstream generateConcaveIndices (earcut) validated on L-shape/violin/collinear — zero out-of-range, areas match shoelace; preferred path taken (useFaceSegmentsConcaveSource for concave families, fan useFaceSegmentsSource for convex), no custom triangulator. owners expanded then stripped (no-owners RenderTree test added). Fixed concatPacked owner double-rebase bug. Full check clean, 250 core + 5 site + 15/15 visual green, fixtures deterministic. Census: 56 Polygon marks → 20 ChunkedFace; guide/theme Polygon untouched. Verified by orchestrator.

title: Convert point and line mark families to flat tensors, one node per layer
description:
STAGE 3a of epic gggplot-tzc. Blocked by tzc.1, tzc.2. Complete and final (third-pass: EXPLICIT COMPONENT NAMES — chunked marks get their own ComponentName; guides/annotations keep plain Line).

SCOPE — packages/core/src/geom/: point.ts (point, dotplot), line.ts (line, path, step), segment.ts, curve.ts, spoke.ts, rug.ts, refline.ts (hline/vline/abline), errorbar.ts stems (boxes are tzc.4), smooth.ts fitted line (SE ribbon is tzc.4), text.ts POSITIONS and per-row numeric attrs (label strings stay plain). hex.ts is tzc.4's.

COMPONENT NAMING (final design, applies epic-wide; live and emitted backends MUST match): RenderTree component names are semantic. A mark node carrying chunked flat topology uses the NEW ComponentName 'ChunkedLine' (this bead) / 'ChunkedFace' (tzc.4), added to rendertree.ts's ComponentName union. Plain 'Line'/'Point'/'Polygon' names remain for guides, annotations, reference lines, and any node without MarkTopology — the global REGISTRY mapping for 'Line' is untouched, so guide/axis lines cannot be affected by mark changes. The live REGISTRY decides ChunkedLine's REALIZATION once: if the spike (below) shows plot Line natively consumes our positions tensor + chunk encoding, ChunkedLine's registry entry simply delegates to plot Line; otherwise it is a wrapper on workbench LineLayer + useLineSegmentsSource({chunks, loops}) (resident_bar.tsx pattern). Either way the NAME stays 'ChunkedLine' so RenderTree semantics and emission stay transparent. MANDATORY TEST: a spec with a grouped geom line AND an hline annotation — the geom lowers to ChunkedLine, the annotation stays Line.

RULE: one node per RENDERER-COMPATIBLE STYLE BATCH per layer. Sanctioned batches here: per-shape Point splits (shape is a uniform trait), per-dash-pattern Line splits. Inline comment naming this bead on each; tzc.8's budget test enumerates exactly these.

POINT (lowerPoint): positions FlatTensor(vec2) + topology {kind:'points'} via packMarkRows; colors FlatTensor(vec4) with per-row alpha folded (DELETE the rgbaColors string path); sizes/strokes FlatTensor(f32). Keep the two-node stroke-outline fallback, flat. Repeat tzc.1's mid-data alignment test for point with mapped color+size and NaN y mid-column. Component name stays 'Point' (points topology needs no chunk realization decision).

LINE (lowerLine): ONE ChunkedLine node per layer (per dash batch): pack each group, concatPacked -> positions tensor + topology {kind:'polyline', chunks, loops:false}; per-group color repeated per vertex. SPIKE FIRST (recorded in notes): does plot Line accept our explicit chunk topology via tensors? Outcome selects ChunkedLine's registry realization as described above.

COORDINATES: emit flat nodes with topology; NO polar handling here — tzc.2 owns it. Polar line routes legitimately change (curved chords); inspect those visual diffs deliberately.

FIXTURES: regenerate; diffs confined to converted families + polar line routes; review the diff.

Do NOT touch bar/area/tile/polygon/hex families, emit/mod.ts, or the resident path.
acceptance_criteria: deno task check; core tests green after intentional regen; site tests + test:visual green (separated multi-series lines; curved polar chords); 3-group solid-dash line layer -> exactly 1 ChunkedLine node; hline annotation remains component 'Line' (mandatory guide-vs-mark test); point alignment test passes; spike outcome + chosen realization recorded in notes.
notes:
AMENDMENTS (2026-07-18 design review on epic gggplot-tzc):
1. SCOPE ADDITIONS: also convert smooth.ts (the fitted-line part; its SE ribbon moves with tzc.4) and text.ts POSITIONS (label strings stay plain string arrays — only per-row numeric attrs like positions/sizes/angles go flat, per the epic's revised scope rule). rug.ts/spoke.ts/refline.ts were already in scope; confirm hex.ts is NOT here (it is tzc.4's).
2. NODE-SPLIT LANGUAGE: the rule is 'one node per renderer-compatible style batch per layer'. Sanctioned batches: per-shape Point splits, per-dash-pattern Line splits. Both must carry an inline comment naming this bead, and tzc.8's budget test enumerates exactly these. Do not introduce other splits without adding them to that test with justification.
3. ROW ALIGNMENT: use tzc.1's packMarkRows single-mask entry point exclusively; never call individual packers with self-computed masks. The mid-data invalid-row alignment test pattern from tzc.1 must be repeated for at least one geom here (point with mapped color+size and a NaN y mid-column).
4. TOPOLOGY: emit MarkTopology ({kind:'polyline', chunks: Uint32Array}) per tzc.1's revised contract — no ragged field on tensors. The Line spike now tests whether plot Line accepts positions tensor + explicit segment encoding; if not, ChunkedLine via workbench LineLayer + useLineSegmentsSource({chunks, loops}) is the default path, not the fallback.
5. LOWERING ORDER: emit flat nodes with topology BEFORE any coordinate concern; polarize/munch (tzc.2) dispatches on topology metadata, so do not special-case polar here at all.
SPIKE RESULT: plot's native <Line> (traits.mjs SegmentsTrait) does NOT natively accept an explicit variable-length chunk list over a flat FlatTensor 'positions' prop. title: Epic: flat-array GPU-centric mark pipeline
description:
Move the entire non-resident mark path from 'nested JS arrays in JSX props' to flat typed-array tensors that Use.GPU uploads once and reconciles by identity. Implements GPU_NATIVE_ARCHITECTURE_PLAN.md Phase 2 and starts Phase 3, per docs/REVIEW_2026-07-18_SECOND_PASS.md §2.3-2.4. Revised through three design reviews (see notes); CHILD DESCRIPTIONS ARE AUTHORITATIVE AND SELF-CONTAINED — notes are history, not overrides.

VERIFIED FACTS (do not re-litigate):
- @use-gpu/plot's Point/Line/Face accept TensorArray ({array: TypedArray, format, dims, length, size, version?}; node_modules/@use-gpu/core/mjs/types.d.mts:351) for positions/colors/widths/sizes, alongside ShaderSource handles. Upstream TensorArray.ragged is (number[]|TypedArray)[] grouping arrays — we do NOT use it; topology travels separately (MarkTopology, tzc.1).
- Chunked-primitive path: workbench FaceLayer + useFaceSegmentsSource (proven in runtime/resident_bar.tsx) and LineLayer + useLineSegmentsSource({chunks, groups, loops}) (line-segments.mjs:19); loops accepts boolean | boolean[] upstream.
- CONCAVE faces supported upstream: getFaceSegmentsConcave / useFaceSegmentsConcaveSource backed by generateConcaveIndices (face-segments.mjs:17,41). tzc.4 spikes this before any custom triangulation.

COMPONENT-NAMING DECISION (third review, final): chunked marks are DISTINCT ComponentNames — 'ChunkedLine' (tzc.3), 'ChunkedFace' (tzc.4). Plain Line/Point/Polygon names remain for guides/annotations/background, so mark realization changes cannot affect guide rendering. Live REGISTRY and emitSource choose the same realization once.

EXECUTION ORDER (matches the dependency graph exactly): tzc.1 -> tzc.2 -> {tzc.3, tzc.4 in parallel} -> then {tzc.5, tzc.6 in parallel — tzc.6 needs only tzc.3+tzc.4} -> tzc.7 (needs tzc.5) -> tzc.8 (needs tzc.5+tzc.6+tzc.7) closes the epic.

DESIGN REVIEW — 2026-07-18

Overall: direction is sound, but revise the contract and dependency graph before implementation to avoid redesign during tzc.2–tzc.5.

Critical corrections:
1. TensorArray.ragged is not a simple chunk-length vector. The installed Use.GPU type models ragged as grouping/dimension arrays, while Line/Face paths also use explicit chunks/groups/loops/segments. Keep FlatTensor compatible with upstream TensorArray and define separate integer topology buffers (for example chunks/groups/loops) unless the spikes prove an exact supported ragged encoding.
2. Independent packers can break row alignment. packPositions proposes dropping non-finite pairs while colors/sizes/strokes may retain those rows. Use a shared retained-row mask, a packMarkRows operation, or a defined sentinel policy. Add a test with an invalid coordinate in the middle of mapped color/size data.
3. Current munchPolygonNode only processes component === "Polygon". Converting geometry to Face before coordinate munching bypasses it. Specify an execution order: preferably transform/munch logical geometry before lowering to renderer components, or explicitly make Face topology coordinate-aware.
4. Phase 3 does not yet prove zero re-pack/re-upload. Memoizing compile by [spec,width,height,measureText] is invalidated by a changed scale-domain/spec identity. Numeric equality of raw positions is insufficient; require reference identity or upload/allocation instrumentation across domain changes, backed by a data/mark cache, independently memoized packing stage, or resident GPU source.

Scope/acceptance corrections:
- Narrow “every mark attribute is FlatTensor” to every per-row numeric/vector mark attribute. Uniform, textual, and structural props should remain scalar/metadata.
- Do not restrict all storage to Float32Array: topology/index/group buffers naturally require integer TypedArrays. Separate float attributes from integer topology or use upstream TypedArray.
- Audit and assign ownership for nested positions in hex.ts, smooth.ts, text.ts, rug.ts, spoke.ts, and refline.ts in addition to the files already named. Text values stay textual, but text positions/numeric attributes should follow the flat contract.
- Define how munching expands companion attributes: interpolation vs repetition for continuous color, categorical color, size, opacity, and the closing edge.
- Resolve concave polygons explicitly using the supported concave path, triangulated indices, ChunkedFace, or a documented exception. A fallback to existing nested Polygon conflicts with the epic-wide acceptance criteria.
- Reconcile node-count exceptions: child plans permit line splitting for incompatible dash patterns, while the epic permits only per-shape Point splitting. Prefer “one node per renderer-compatible style batch,” with explicit point-shape and dash/topology exceptions.
- Test memoization at its actual abstraction. React useMemo only preserves results within one mounted component; two direct compile() calls will not become ===. Either mount the Live component or extract a separately testable compile/packing cache. Test tensor identity separately from RenderTree identity.
- Add runtime/browser instrumentation for GPU buffer/source creation and upload/update calls. CPU compile time, byte counts, and node counts alone do not prove the epic’s no-reupload claim.
- Split performance measurements into packing, coordinate transformation/munching, RenderTree construction, emission, and GPU initialization/upload. Bound iterations/warmup for the 1M-row case.

Dependency correction:
tzc.8 currently depends only on tzc.5, so it can close the epic before tzc.6 and tzc.7 finish. Make tzc.8 depend on tzc.5, tzc.6, and tzc.7. Intended shape:
tzc.1 -> tzc.2 -> {tzc.3, tzc.4} -> tzc.5;
{tzc.3, tzc.4} -> tzc.6;
tzc.5 -> tzc.7;
{tzc.5, tzc.6, tzc.7} -> tzc.8/epic closure.

Recommended revision order:
(1) correct tensor/topology and retained-row contracts in tzc.1;
(2) define coordinate-munch semantics and lowering order in tzc.2;
(3) complete emitter ownership and concavity/style-batch exceptions in tzc.3/.4;
(4) clarify cache boundary and identity tests in tzc.5/.7;
(5) strengthen runtime upload/performance gates and dependencies in tzc.8.
RESPONSE TO DESIGN REVIEW (2026-07-18): all findings accepted and folded in. (1) FlatTensor no longer models upstream ragged; topology is a separate MarkTopology with integer TypedArrays (chunks/loops/indices) — tzc.1 rewritten. (2) Row alignment: single-mask packMarkRows entry point + mandatory mid-data invalid-row test — tzc.1/tzc.3. (3) Coordinate stage now dispatches on topology metadata, not component name; lowering-order contract added (loops -> polarize/munch -> indices), munch rejects pre-indexed nodes — tzc.2/tzc.4. (4) Zero re-pack proof upgraded from useMemo to an explicit testable PackCache with domain-excluded keys for eligible axes; reference identity required across rebuilt specs — tzc.5/tzc.7 rewritten. (5) Scope narrowed to per-row numeric/vector attrs; integer buffers allowed. (6) hex/smooth/text/rug/spoke/refline ownership assigned (tzc.3: smooth line, text positions; tzc.4: hex, smooth ribbon). (7) Munch companion policy: repetition of segment start vertex, no interpolation, documented. (8) Concavity: earcut indices + ChunkedFace; nested-Polygon fallback withdrawn. (9) Node-count rule: one node per renderer-compatible style batch with enumerated exceptions. (10) Memoization tested at the cache boundary, not mounted components. (11) tzc.8 gains GPU createBuffer/writeBuffer instrumentation and staged, bounded benches. (12) Deps fixed: tzc.8 now blocked by tzc.5+tzc.6+tzc.7.

SECOND-PASS DESIGN REVIEW — 2026-07-18

Overall: the revised epic is substantially better and close to implementable. The dependency graph is now correct, and the tensor/topology separation, aligned-row packing, concavity policy, and cache-boundary tests resolve the main first-pass concerns. Remaining issues:

IMPORTANT:
1. CONSOLIDATE THE OPERATIVE TEXT. Several descriptions still contradict their amendments: tzc.3/.4 describe ragged tensors; tzc.4 still permits nested Polygon fallback; tzc.6's example emits ragged; tzc.7 still permits numeric equality. Rewrite each description and acceptance criteria to contain only the final design. Keep historical review material in notes, but do not require implementers to infer that notes override descriptions.
2. CORRECT THE MEMORY-LAYOUT TERM. tzc.1 says FloatTensor is “component-major,” but the stride-2 design and Use.GPU vector inputs require interleaved/row-major components: [x0,y0,x1,y1,...], not [all x..., all y...]. Change the contract wording and add a small explicit layout test.
3. CACHE DERIVED GEOMETRY, NOT ONLY packMarkRows. tzc.2 allocates new arrays during polarize/munch, and tzc.4 creates triangulated index buffers after transforms. A cache only around initial packing cannot make final renderer tensors/topology reference-identical across compiles and may still cause GPU re-upload. Cache renderer-ready PackedMark results or use staged caches keyed by input tensor identity plus coordinate/topology parameters. Add === tests for Cartesian points, grouped-line topology, polar/munched geometry, and concave triangulated Face.
4. DEFINE GPU-UPLOAD ATTRIBUTION. Wrapping every GPUDevice.createBuffer/GPUQueue.writeBuffer cannot distinguish mark data from legitimate view, guide, uniform, canvas, or transient work. A scale-domain change may correctly write a uniform. Define how tzc.8 recognizes mark-data operations: stable buffer labels, instrumentation at Use.GPU raw-source creation/update, debug tags on FlatTensor-derived sources, or tracked mark-buffer identities. Assert zero MARK-DATA upload, not zero GPU writes globally.

ADDITIONAL LOGICAL GAPS:
5. tzc.2 says munching applies to loops AND polylines, then says polyline is passthrough. Choose one. Prefer implementing nonlinear-coordinate polyline subdivision here; otherwise explicitly exclude it and create/document follow-up work.
6. PackCache needs a data-mutation policy. WeakMap keys based on column-array identity become stale if arrays mutate in place, while FlatTensor.version is always 0. State/enforce immutable ingested columns, introduce a source revision, or provide explicit invalidation. At minimum document immutable-input cache semantics and test them.
7. MarkTopology.loops is only boolean, while Use.GPU line segments accept boolean | boolean[]. Either support per-chunk loop flags or guarantee homogeneous open/closed topology per renderer node.
8. Spike existing Use.GPU concave support before writing a custom triangulator. Workbench already exposes getFaceSegmentsConcave/useFaceSegmentsConcaveSource backed by generateConcaveIndices. Reuse it if viable; if not, document why. Also call a no-holes ear-clipping implementation “ear clipping,” not “earcut.”
9. packMarkRows is point-centric. Bars/areas/ribbons/boxplots/polygons expand a source row into multiple vertices. Define source-row selection separately from source-row-to-vertex expansion, or let geometry packing carry vertex-owner indices so all per-row attributes expand deterministically.

tzc.1 -> tzc.2 -> {tzc.3, tzc.4} -> tzc.5;
{tzc.3, tzc.4} -> tzc.6;
tzc.5 -> tzc.7;
{tzc.5, tzc.6, tzc.7} -> tzc.8/epic closure.

RECOMMENDED FINAL REVISION BEFORE tzc.1:
(1) fold amendments into descriptions/acceptance criteria;
(2) fix tensor-layout terminology;
(3) extend caching through renderer-ready derived buffers;
(4) specify upload attribution;
(5) settle polyline munching and immutable-data semantics;
(6) spike Use.GPU concave support before committing to custom triangulation.
RESPONSE TO SECOND-PASS REVIEW (2026-07-18): all 9 findings accepted; every child description rewritten to be self-contained and final (notes are now history only — this was finding 1 and governs how implementers read these beads). Specifics: (2) 'component-major' corrected to INTERLEAVED with an explicit layout test in tzc.1. (3) tzc.5 is now a STAGED geometry cache (pack -> coordinate/topology -> derived indices) whose stage outputs are the tensors placed on RenderTree nodes; === tests required for all four geometry classes (cartesian points, grouped-line topology, polar munched, concave face). (4) tzc.8 attributes MARK-DATA uploads by registering tensor arrays at the source boundary and counting only matching createBuffer/writeBuffer payloads; uniform/guide writes are explicitly permitted. (5) Polyline munching is now IMPLEMENTED in tzc.2 (closing-edge distinction specified; ARCHITECTURE.md known-gap note retired when it lands). (6) Data-mutation policy: ingested columns immutable by contract (documented in data/mod.ts), version stays 0, packCache.invalidate() escape hatch. (7) loops stays boolean with a documented per-node topological-homogeneity constraint (upstream boolean[] noted, unneeded — no geom family mixes). (8) Verified upstream concave support exists (getFaceSegmentsConcave/useFaceSegmentsConcaveSource/generateConcaveIndices, face-segments.mjs:17,41); tzc.4 now spikes it FIRST and custom ear clipping (renamed from earcut) is the documented-failure path only. (9) packMarkRows split into source-row selection vs row-to-vertex expansion via MarkTopology.owners + expandByOwners in tzc.1. Epic description/acceptance updated to match (interleaved, renderer-ready identity, attributed uploads, homogeneous topology, upstream-concave-first).

THIRD/FINAL DESIGN REVIEW — 2026-07-18

Overall: the epic is coherent and substantially implementation-ready. Earlier contract, scope, dependency, coordinate-ordering, and staged-cache issues are resolved. Three execution clarifications remain:

1. MAKE RENDERER COMPONENT SELECTION UNAMBIGUOUS. tzc.3 currently says RenderTree always emits component "Line" and the live REGISTRY decides whether it is Plot Line or ChunkedLine. The registry maps component names globally, so replacing Line could also affect guides/axes/annotations without MarkTopology. The emitted backend has the same ambiguity: it may print <Line> from @use-gpu/plot even when only ChunkedLine understands explicit chunks. Choose one final design: (a) explicit ChunkedLine/ChunkedFace ComponentName values, preferred for transparent RenderTree semantics and simple emission; (b) adaptive Line/Face wrappers that inspect props.topology and delegate; or (c) normalize to final renderer component names before emission. Add a test that ordinary guide/annotation lines still use Plot Line while grouped geom lines use the topology-aware path. Live and emitted backends must make the same choice.

2. KEEP owners AS COMPILER BOOKKEEPING UNLESS THE RENDERER NEEDS IT. owners exists to expand source-row attributes into vertex attributes; after expandByOwners, it is not renderer topology. Carrying it in final MarkTopology and emitted source enlarges trees/modules, adds another identity obligation, and risks accidental GPU-source treatment. Prefer an internal PackedGeometry {topology, owners?}; perform expansion; strip owners before renderer-facing MarkTopology. Stage-A cache tests may still verify owner identity. Only retain/emit owners if a concrete later renderer stage demonstrably consumes it.

3. DEFINE AN IMPLEMENTABLE MULTI-COLUMN CACHE INVALIDATION STRUCTURE. A WeakMap rooted on one column cannot invalidate entries reached through a different dependent column without a reverse index; a strong reverse index can defeat GC. Preferred approach: WeakMap<column, revision>, include every dependent column's revision in the stage key, and invalidate(column) increments its revision. Alternatively use ordered nested WeakMaps and permit whole-cache invalidation. Exact fine-grained invalidation is optional; correctness and weak reachability are mandatory. Test a mark mapped to x/y/color/size: invalidate color; color changes, position may remain === if independently cached, and unrelated-layer tensors remain ===.

- Label tzc.4's obsolete custom-triangulation notes explicitly historical to avoid conflict with its authoritative upstream-concave-first description.
- In tzc.8, ArrayBuffer payload matching can help attribute writeBuffer, but cannot attribute createBuffer because createBuffer receives only a descriptor. Make source-boundary tagging/instrumentation the required create attribution mechanism; payload matching is optional write attribution.

FINAL READINESS VERDICT: after resolving explicit/adaptive chunked component naming, compile-only owners, and the multi-column invalidation structure, gggplot-tzc is ready to execute in its stated dependency order.

title: Split compile/lowering.ts into per-geom modules with registry dispatch
description:
## Context

`packages/core/src/compile/lowering.ts` is 1,769 lines (~16% of core) and holds ~20 private `lowerXxxLayer` functions, shared aesthetic-extraction helpers, and a ~400-line `lowerLayer` dispatcher (line 1355) built as a cascade of `if (layer.geom === ...)` blocks. Some geoms (area/ribbon, point, line/path/step) are lowered inline inside the dispatcher rather than in named functions. Meanwhile the stat side (`packages/core/src/stat/mod.ts`) already uses the right pattern: a `Record<StatKind, StatFn>` registry with a uniform function contract and implementations in focused modules. This issue makes the geom side mirror that pattern with one file per geom, like ggplot2's `geom-*.R` layout.

A second problem fixed here: `lowerLayer` takes 19 positional parameters, 8 of which are individual trained scales (colorScale, fillScale, sizeScale, alphaScale, shapeScale, linetypeScale, linewidthScale, strokeScale). `compile()` in `packages/core/src/compile/mod.ts` destructures the same scales positionally and threads them through `buildPanel`, `guideLayout`, and `legendNodes`. Every new aesthetic touches a dozen signatures.

Note: `packages/core/src/geom/` already exists but contains only `bar_grid.ts` (a GPU ProductPlan for histogram bar topology). This refactor makes `geom/` the real home for geoms; `bar_grid.ts` content moves into (or next to) `geom/bar.ts`.

## Target structure

```
packages/core/src/geom/
├── mod.ts        # GEOM_REGISTRY: Record<GeomKind, GeomDefinition>; exports lowerLayer(layer, mapping, data, ctx)
├── types.ts      # GeomDefinition and LayerContext interfaces
├── shared.ts     # helpers moved from lowering.ts: valuesOf, positionsOf, sortByX, colorsOf,
│                 #   sizesOf, alphasOf, colorWithAlpha, shapesOf, linewidthsOf, strokesOf,
│                 #   dashOf, literalLineProps, bandPositions, resolutionOf, requiredValues,
│                 #   stepPositions, normalizeFontface
├── point.ts, line.ts (line/path/step), bar.ts (bar/col + bar_grid GPU plan), area.ts (area/ribbon
│   + silhouette), tile.ts, hex.ts, polygon.ts, errorbar.ts (errorbar/linerange/pointrange/
│   crossbar), boxplot.ts, violin.ts, text.ts (text/label), segment.ts, rect.ts,
│   refline.ts (hline/vline/abline), curve.ts, spoke.ts, rug.ts, blank.ts, smooth.ts
```

Grouping related kinds in one file (e.g. errorbar family) is fine — the registry maps each `GeomKind` to its definition; files may export several.

```ts
// geom/types.ts
export interface LayerContext {
  scales: Partial<Record<AesName, TrainedScale>>;  // replaces 8 positional scale params
  theme: Theme;
  xDomain: [number, number];
  yDomain: [number, number];
  panelPixels: { width: number; height: number };
  measureText?: TextMeasurer;
}

export interface GeomDefinition {
  /** default stat/position used by the DSL layer builder */
  defaultStat: StatKind;
  defaultPosition?: PositionKind;   // default "identity"
  lower(layer: Layer, mapping: Aes, data: DataFrame, ctx: LayerContext): RenderNode[];
  // domainContribution? and residentPlan? hooks are added by follow-up issues
  // (gggplot beads: domain-widening hooks; resident capability declarations) —
  // declare the interface fields optional now if convenient, but do not wire them.
}
```

## Steps

1. Create `geom/types.ts` and `geom/shared.ts`; move the shared helpers listed above out of `lowering.ts` verbatim (they are pure functions; keep exports that `compile/mod.ts` uses today: `valuesOf`, `resolutionOf`, `lowerLayer`, `normalizeFontface`, `colorWithAlpha` — re-export from `geom/mod.ts` and keep `compile/mod.ts` + `compile/lowering.ts` import sites working, or update importers).
2. Move each `lowerXxxLayer` into its per-geom file, converting its signature to `(layer, mapping, data, ctx)` and reading scales via `ctx.scales.color` etc. Extract the inline dispatcher bodies (point, line/path/step, area/ribbon) into named functions in their files.
3. Build `GEOM_REGISTRY` in `geom/mod.ts` and reimplement `lowerLayer` as a lookup + call (blank maps to a definition whose `lower` returns `[]`). No if-chain.
4. Update `compile/mod.ts`: build one `LayerContext` per panel (it already computes all inputs) and pass it through `buildPanel` → `lowerLayer`. Keep `guideLayout`/`legendNodes` signatures unchanged in this issue (or pass the scales record if the change is contained — reviewer's choice; do not let this issue sprawl into guides).
5. Regenerate `dsl/geoms.ts` defaults from the registry: each DSL constructor currently hardcodes `geom(kind, defaultStat, opts, defaultPosition?)`. Either derive the constructors mechanically from `GEOM_REGISTRY` keys + a name map, or (smaller diff) keep explicit constructors but source defaultStat/defaultPosition from the registry so there is a single source of truth. Preserve the exact exported constructor names — the docs coverage test (`apps/site/src/docs/geom_coverage_test.ts`) asserts a bijection against them.
6. Delete `compile/lowering.ts` once empty; keep a re-export shim only if external packages import from it (grep `apps/` and `packages/` for `compile/lowering`).
7. Move `geom/bar_grid.ts`'s `createHistogramBarTopologyPlan` into/next to `geom/bar.ts`; update the import in whatever references it (grep for `bar_grid`).

## Constraints

- Pure refactor: zero behavior change. The RenderTree emitted for every existing test fixture and docs example must be identical (deep-equal) before/after.
- Follow existing code style (Deno, no default exports, doc comments explaining constraints).
- Do not modify `stat/`, `scale/`, `position/` beyond import paths.

## Verification

- `deno task check` (or `deno check`) and full test suite: `deno test` across packages/core and apps/site.
- Add a snapshot-style test if one doesn't exist: compile 3–4 representative specs (bar+stack, faceted point, polar, text) and assert the RenderTree JSON matches pre-refactor output (capture fixtures before starting).
- `apps/site` visual smoke: `apps/site/scripts/visual_smoke.ts` per repo conventions.
acceptance_criteria: compile/lowering.ts is gone (or a thin re-export shim); each geom's lowering lives in packages/core/src/geom/<name>.ts; lowerLayer dispatches via Record<GeomKind, GeomDefinition> with no geom if-chain; lowerLayer/compile pass a LayerContext object instead of 8 positional scale params; DSL constructors source defaultStat/defaultPosition from the registry with exported names unchanged; RenderTree output is deep-equal to pre-refactor fixtures; all deno checks/tests and the site visual smoke pass.
notes: Refactor complete on refactor/geom-registry. Split compile/lowering.ts (deleted) into packages/core/src/geom/*.ts, one file per geom family. Dispatch via GEOM_REGISTRY: Record<GeomKind, GeomDefinition> in geom/mod.ts (mirrors stat/mod.ts). LayerContext object (geom/types.ts) replaces the 19-positional-param lowerLayer signature; built once per panel in compile/mod.ts buildPanel. Pure helpers moved verbatim to geom/shared.ts (re-exported from geom/mod.ts for compile importers). bar_grid.ts merged into geom/bar.ts. DSL geom() helper now sources defaultStat/defaultPosition from GEOM_REGISTRY; constructor names unchanged (coverage bijection test passes). Verified: byte-identical RenderTree for 10 fixtures (scripts/capture_geom_fixtures.ts, fixtures under tests/fixtures/geom_registry/), deno task check, core 208 + site 5 tests pass, visual_smoke passed on representations/stats/positions/aesthetics routes. Pure refactor, zero behavior change; no bugs found.
close_reason: Implemented and verified on refactor/geom-registry @ bc4e6cc: per-geom modules + GEOM_REGISTRY dispatch + LayerContext; 208 core tests, 10/10 RenderTree fixtures deep-equal, coverage bijection pass

title: Fix duplicate view-uniform binding in rotated labels
description:
## Problem
The Themes gallery route emits a WebGPU shader validation error: rotated Label composition references two transform/cartesian view-uniform variables at @group(0) @binding(0), invalidating the label pipeline. Ordinary labels and marks still render, which can hide the failure.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run deno task dev and open http://localhost:8081/#themes in a WebGPU browser.
2. Wait for the Theme examples to mount.
3. Inspect console: UIRender vertex/label reports entry point main references multiple variables using @group(0) @binding(0), with a transform chain containing two transform/cartesian stages.

## Scope
Trace RotatedLabel/useCombinedMatrixTransform composition relative to PanelViewport/Cartesian and remove the duplicate view transform without losing GPU-native rotation.
design: Keep rotation in the single UseGPU canvas and avoid composing two shader modules that both declare the same view-uniform binding. Prefer one transform stage with rotation folded into positions/layout over suppressing validation.
acceptance_criteria: Themes route renders rotated labels with no shader or pipeline validation errors; ordinary and faceted labels remain visible; rotation angle and placement are preserved; a focused structural/runtime regression covers one rotated axis/text label; full tests, build, and themes visual smoke pass.
notes: Root cause: RotatedLabel copied @use-gpu/wgsl/use/view into a separately loaded module, producing a second PASS(0)/binding(0) ViewUniforms declaration when Cartesian transforms were linked. Replaced the copy with canonical getViewResolution/getWorldScale/worldToClip exports from @use-gpu/wgsl/use/view.wgsl and added the scoped Deno import mapping. Validation: 194 tests pass; deno task check/build pass; clean browser #themes has no shader errors; visual_smoke --route=themes passes.
close_reason: Canonical shared WGSL view symbols eliminate duplicate uniform binding; validated tests, build, browser, and visual smoke.

title: Eliminate legend key, glyph, and label pixel collisions
description:

The user reports overlapping legend pixels. The compiler also contains fixed guide spacing (including a 44px horizontal allowance and normalized vertical increments), but no captured minimal fixture yet proves which path causes the report.

## Steps to Reproduce

2. Determine whether the collision occurs in the default gallery or only synthetic extremes.
3. Inspect horizontal reservation and vertical row/title placement separately.
4. If the default supported gallery does not reproduce, downgrade this bead to P2 before implementation.

## Scope
Once reproduced, implement measured layout for the failing discrete guide path. File a separate bead for continuous colorbar/steps/bins if it uses a materially different layout path. Define minimum supported canvas width and one long-label policy before changing code.
design: Introduce explicit guide key box, text extent, title/row gaps, padding, and glyph bounds in CSS layout pixels. Document whether long labels wrap, truncate, or expand the guide. Convert to physical pixels only at the canvas boundary after demonstrating any DPR effect.
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in minimal fixture captures the pre-fix collision; the supported minimum canvas width and overflow policy are documented; key, title, row, and glyph bounds have explicit measurable dimensions; the fixture has no overlapping occupied pixel bounds after repair; ordinary color/fill/shape/linetype/size legends retain expected output; browser regression coverage includes the reported viewport and one narrow supported viewport.
notes: Reproduced in the default Color-mapped scatter at a 471x360 chart: categorical point swatches overlapped the first pixels of labels cyl 4/6/8. Cause: swatchX and labelX were fractions of the remaining guide margin, so spacing shrank below the key radius. Fix uses an explicit 20px key box, 8px guide padding, and 6px label gap converted once to normalized coordinates. Added a 471px regression asserting 16px center-to-label spacing. Browser shows clean separation/no console errors; 194 tests, build, check, and guides visual smoke pass.

title: Restore marks and strips in Live faceted plots
description:
## Problem
P1 regression reproduced on 2026-07-17 at http://localhost:8081/#facets: facet_wrap and facet_grid emit outer axes/ticks but no points or bars, and strip labels/panel structure are absent. Non-faceted plots render marks in the same host. Static RenderTree tests do not exercise the failing Live rendering path.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run deno task dev and open http://localhost:8081/#facets in a WebGPU browser.
2. At the default gallery viewport, inspect Faceted scatter: eight source rows should produce eight visible points distributed across three facet panels, but no points or strips are visible.
3. Inspect Facet grid with per-panel stats: counted bars and crossed panels are absent.
4. Record browser/OS, viewport, DPR, console diagnostics, and a screenshot before changing code.

## Scope
Trace the Live tree from compiled panel nodes through context providers and virtual-layer submission; identify the first lost mark/label binding; make the smallest repair; add a browser-level regression. The difference between Live FacetPanel context setup and emitted-source Embedded panels is a hypothesis to test, not an assumed cause. Broader strip/axis/free-scale/responsive layout semantics belong in a separate bead.
design: Keep one top-level canvas. Preserve the intended fixed-facet axis policy unless evidence requires changing it. Runtime and emitted backends may use different mechanics, but must produce equivalent plot semantics.
acceptance_criteria: The two existing gallery facet examples visibly render their expected marks and strip labels at the recorded fixture; no new console/render errors occur; non-faceted plots remain unchanged; a browser visual or pixel regression fails on the pre-fix blank output and passes after repair; the root cause and why RenderTree-only tests missed it are recorded.
notes: Root cause: FacetGrid computed cell rectangles in ambient pixel layout, then installed matrix/range contexts inside the outer normalized Embedded. This bypassed the one layout-bearing virtual-layer submission path, so panel marks vanished. Nested/sibling Embedded experiments rendered marks but produced zero-sized GPU bindings. Final repair keeps one outer Embedded and gives each facet a normalized PanelViewport matrix; strip labels render in the shared plot overlay. title: Stat/group pipeline ignores implicit grouping and per-group aggregation
description:
Confirmed via direct repro against compile(): our stat pipeline and line/path/area/ribbon group-splitting only ever look at an EXPLICIT mapping.group column. ggplot2's real rule is that group defaults to the interaction of every discrete aesthetic mapped on the layer (color/fill/shape/linetype), not just group=. This breaks three extremely common ggplot2 idioms silently (no warning, wrong-looking chart):

1. geom_line(aes(x=x, y=y, color=g)) with no explicit group= draws ONE zigzagging line across all groups interleaved by x, instead of one clean line per color group. Repro: ggplot({x:[0,1,2,0,1,2], y:[1,2,3,10,20,30], g:['a','a','a','b','b','b']}, {x:'x',y:'y',color:'g'}).add(geomLine()) -> compile() produces a single Line node with positions [[0,1],[0,10],[1,2],[1,20],[2,3],[2,30]] (interleaved/zigzag) instead of two Line nodes.

2. geom_bar()/geom_histogram() with fill mapped to a sub-category (e.g. ggplot(mpg, aes(class, fill=drv)) + geom_bar()) doesn't stack by fill at all -- stat_count (stat/mod.ts) counts by x only and returns a brand-new data object containing ONLY [xCol] and 'count', silently dropping the fill/color/group column entirely. Downstream lowerBarLayer (compile/mod.ts) then can't find the dropped column so falls back to a single solid-fill bar per x showing the total count. Repro confirmed: geomBar() with {x:'cls', fill:'drv'} on 5 rows (a:2x'f'+1x'4', b:2x'4') renders two solid #2a78d6 Polygon segments with no stacking and no legend, instead of stacked color segments.

3. geom_smooth(aes(color=g)) fits ONE trend line pooling all groups' data together (statSmooth in stat/mod.ts has zero group-awareness), instead of one fitted line per group. Repro confirmed: 2 groups with opposite slopes (flat vs steep) produce a single blended Line node, not 2.

Root cause is shared: applyStat and splitByGroup both only consult mapping.group, and stat functions (statCount/statBin/statSummary) discard every column except the ones they explicitly re-emit, so even a downstream per-group split has nothing left to split on. Needs (a) a shared 'effective group key' resolver used everywhere group-splitting happens (aes group ?? interaction of mapped discrete color/fill/shape/linetype), and (b) stat_count/stat_bin/stat_summary/stat_smooth reworked to aggregate/fit PER effective-group instead of over the whole layer, preserving the group-defining column(s) in their output data.
acceptance_criteria: geom_line/path/area/ribbon with only color or fill mapped (no explicit group=) render one connected shape per distinct color/fill level, matching ggplot2. geom_bar()/geom_histogram() with fill mapped to a discrete sub-category stack/dodge counts correctly per (x, fill) combination and emit a fill legend. geom_smooth()/stat_summary() fit/aggregate independently per effective group when color/fill/group is mapped. New pipeline_test.ts cases cover all three scenarios above (they should currently fail before the fix).
close_reason: Implemented shared effective-group resolver and grouped stat/render fixes for line/path/area/ribbon, stat_count/stat_bin, stat_summary, and geom_smooth/stat_smooth with regression coverage.

title: ChunkedLine renders solid regardless of dash pattern
description: Surfaced during gggplot-tzc.3. ChunkedLine is realized over the workbench raw-line primitive (LineLayer/RawLines + useLineSegmentsSource), which has no dash support. lowerLine correctly batches nodes per dash pattern and threads a 'dash' prop through (satisfying tzc's node-split rule), but the dash value is not rendered — dashed/dotted geom_line/geom_path currently draw solid. Need a dash-capable line realization (e.g. shader-level stroke-dash on the raw line source, or route dashed batches through a dash-capable plot Line path) so per-dash style batches render correctly. Not a silent drop: the topology/prop plumbing already exists; only the visual realization is missing.
notes:
APPROACH DECISION (2026-07-19, user-selected): custom WGSL dash shader (screen-space-correct, reads st arc-length + dash array, discards 'off' fragments). Investigation findings for the implementer: (1) workbench RawLinesProps (primitives/raw-lines.d.mts) — the primitive ChunkedLine renders through — has NO dash uniform (props: position/segment/uv/st/color/width/depth/zBias/trim/size + source variants). It DOES expose st/sts (arc-length) which a dash material can consume. (2) plot's StrokeTrait (plot/mjs/traits.mjs:140) defines dash: optional(parseScalarArray) and plot Line's LineProps has dash?, but NO standalone reusable dash WGSL module was found in @use-gpu/wgsl or workbench — so plot's own dash rendering path must be located and either reused or replicated. (3) tzc.3 spike already established plot Line rejects our variable-length chunk topology, so we can't route dashed batches to plot Line without reintroducing nested arrays (regression). IMPLEMENTER MUST FIRST verify how plot actually renders dash end-to-end (does InnerLine produce visible dashes, via which shader/material?) and report that before authoring new WGSL; reuse Use.GPU's shader-linking machinery (@use-gpu/shader) rather than a bespoke pipeline. lowerLine already batches per dash pattern and threads a 'dash' prop onto the RenderNode — the plumbing exists; only the material is missing.
CHECKPOINT FINDING (before authoring WGSL): traced plot's StrokeTrait 'dash'
end-to-end -- InnerLine (plot/mjs/shape/line.mjs) destructures 'dash' out of
LineTraits into its catch-all 'flags' bag and forwards it into
schemaToArchetype/shape.flags, but grepped every real (non-lodash-false-
-positive) match for "dash" across @use-gpu/workbench/mjs, @use-gpu/plot/mjs,
and every .wgsl module under @use-gpu/wgsl (via each module's sourcemap
sourcesContent, which carries the original un-minified WGSL) and found NO
consumer anywhere -- LINE_SCHEMA, raw-lines.mjs's RawLines primitive (which
ChunkedLine already renders through), and every real fragment/vertex .wgsl
file are dash-blind. Outcome (b): no existing dash module to reuse; plot's
own dash rendering is dead code (typed + threaded, never wired to a shader).
Authored a minimal custom dash fragment material via @use-gpu/shader's
runtime `wgsl` tagged template (the same machinery render/rotated_label.tsx
already uses for a custom vertex shader) -- not a bespoke pipeline: it plugs
into RawLines' EXISTING 'getFragment' link point (workbench's
DEFAULT_MATERIAL_CONTEXT.solid.getFragment, currently getPassThruColor),
overriding it via provide(MaterialContext, ...) scoped to just the dashed
LineLayer element. Reads the per-vertex 'st' arc-length varying (a new
'sts' tensor computed in the live realization from the node's own positions
+ chunks, so RenderTree/fixture output is unchanged) and a small vec4 dash-
pattern uniform, discarding fragments in a gap. Screen-space correctness:
converts the DATA-space arc length to device-pixel-equivalent length inside
the shader via view.wgsl's getWorldScale(1.0, 0.0) -- the exact factor
RawLines' own line width already uses at its default depth -- which is
EXACT (not approximate) under gggplot's orthographic FlatCamera host,
because getWorldScale's only spatially-varying term collapses to a constant
1.0 whenever the projection's perspective row is zero (true by construction
for an orthographic camera), so a single global per-frame evaluation
(rather than a true per-fragment one keyed on unavailable clip-space w) is
correct, responds to future pan/zoom, and needed no vertex-shader surgery.
Implementation done: render/chunked_line.tsx (packDashUniforms,
computeArcLengths, getDashColorSource WGSL module, MaterialContext wiring;
solid lines never call provide(), so they render exactly as before) +
emit/mod.ts (CHUNKED_LINE_SOURCE/imports kept in textual parity). Tests:
packages/core/tests/chunked_line_dash_test.ts (10 new, pure-function +
emit/deno-check coverage). Full verification green: deno task check clean;

errors, including the 'representations' route's MtcarsLineStyles example
(geom_line linetype mapped to two dash levels), which mounts this exact
material in a real headless-Chromium WebGPU context.

title: Perf and conformance gate for the flat pipeline
description:
STAGE 6 of epic gggplot-tzc — final gate and closure. Blocked by tzc.5 AND tzc.6 AND tzc.7. Complete and final (third-pass: source-boundary tagging is the REQUIRED attribution mechanism for buffer creation; payload matching is optional write-side corroboration only — createBuffer receives a descriptor, not data, so payload matching cannot attribute it).

1. BENCH (packages/core/bench/, deno bench like reductions_bench.ts) for point, grouped line, stacked bar at 10k/100k/1M rows, in SEPARATE stages: (a) packing, (b) coordinate transform/munch (polar variant), (c) RenderTree construction, (d) emission. Bound the 1M case with fixed warmup and a hard per-case time budget (document the numbers).
2. GPU MARK-DATA UPLOAD INSTRUMENTATION — attribution mechanism (REQUIRED form): instrument at the SOURCE BOUNDARY where the live backend turns FlatTensor/MarkTopology arrays into Use.GPU sources (the ChunkedLine/ChunkedFace/Point realizations and any raw-source creation they call). Under a dev-only ?instrument flag, that boundary records each (tensor.array -> created source/buffer) association; counters then attribute subsequent buffer creations and writes to MARK DATA via those tracked identities. ArrayBuffer payload matching on writeBuffer MAY corroborate write attribution but is NOT the mechanism of record. Find Use.GPU's raw-source creation/update entry points once and document them in notes. Assertions via the visual-smoke harness or a dedicated instrumented route: (i) N re-renders, unchanged spec -> zero NEW mark-data source/buffer creations and zero mark-data writes; (ii) linear-scale x-domain change (tzc.7) -> same zeros while the frame redraws (uniform/guide writes permitted and uncounted).
3. NODE-BUDGET TEST (packages/core/tests/): fixture spec set; one mark node per renderer-compatible style batch per layer; enumerated exceptions ONLY: per-shape Point splits, per-dash ChunkedLine splits, plus any exception a converted geom documented inline with a bead reference. Anything else fails.
4. NESTED-ARRAY TRIPWIRE: walk every fixture RenderTree; no mark node carries array-of-arrays positions; no node carries an owners key; exemptions (guides/annotations if still nested) enumerated explicitly with a TODO bead reference.
5. Record bench + instrumentation results in docs/PERF_BASELINE.md (date + hardware); update docs/RESIDENCY_MATRIX.md.
6. EPIC CLOSURE: verify every epic acceptance bullet point-by-point in gggplot-tzc notes, then close the epic.
acceptance_criteria: Staged bench recorded with bounded 1M case; source-boundary-tagged instrumentation shows zero mark-data creations/writes on re-render AND on linear-domain change (uniform writes permitted); node-budget + tripwire tests in the default test run; PERF_BASELINE.md committed; epic closed with point-by-point verification.
notes:
USE.GPU RAW-SOURCE ENTRY POINTS (spiked once, per the bead's instruction) — full writeup + real numbers in docs/PERF_BASELINE.md; this note is the permanent record.

CREATE/UPLOAD PRIMITIVES (ultimate patch targets, node_modules/.deno/@use-gpu+core@0.19.0/node_modules/@use-gpu/core/mjs/buffer.mjs):
  - makeDataBuffer(device, data, flags) -> makeTypedBuffer -> device.createBuffer({size, usage, mappedAtCreation}). Descriptor only — NO payload — this is why source-boundary tagging (not payload matching) is the required create-attribution mechanism.
  - uploadBuffer(device, buffer, arrayBufferLike) -> device.queue.writeBuffer(buffer, 0, data, 0, data.byteLength).

MARK-DATA SOURCE BOUNDARY (what render/chunked_line.tsx and render/chunked_face.tsx call directly, node_modules/.deno/@use-gpu+workbench@0.19.0/node_modules/@use-gpu/workbench/mjs/hooks/useRawSource.mjs):
  - useRawSource(array, format, options, size, version) / useRawTensorSource(tensorArray, options): (a) useMemo-creates a GPUBuffer via makeDataBuffer, keyed on [device, byteLength-rounded alloc, flags] — NOT tensor identity, so a same-byte-size re-pack REUSES the buffer object; (b) useMemo-calls uploadBuffer, keyed on [device, format, source, array, buffer, version, ...size] — array IDENTITY is a dependency, so an unchanged tensor.array reference across re-renders skips this useMemo entirely (zero re-upload by construction — exactly what PackCache's tzc.5 reference-identity guarantee is FOR).
  - gpu_instrument.ts's withMarkAttribution brackets exactly these two useRawTensorSource calls (positions/colors/widths in chunked_line.tsx; positions/colors in chunked_face.tsx) plus the topology/segments sources (useLineSegmentsSource, useFaceSegmentsSource, useFaceSegmentsConcaveSource) — any createBuffer/writeBuffer triggered synchronously inside the bracket is counted as mark data.

POINT IS A DIFFERENT, NOT-FULLY-BRACKETABLE PATH: Point does NOT go through useRawTensorSource — REGISTRY maps 'Point' straight to @use-gpu/plot's own <Point> (node_modules/.deno/@use-gpu+plot@0.19.0/node_modules/@use-gpu/plot/mjs/shape/point.mjs: useTraits -> schemaToAttributes/schemaToArchetype from @use-gpu/core -> a LayerReconciler quote(yeet(shapes)) deferred batch). That batch's own raw-source/buffer allocation happens deep inside @use-gpu/plot's internal shape-reconciler pipeline, which is NOT synchronously reachable from our REGISTRY wrapping point the way ChunkedLine/ChunkedFace's own hook bodies are — createElement doesn't execute a component's body immediately, and Point's actual buffer work happens later when Live's fiber runtime processes the batch, on a call stack we don't control. CONSEQUENCE: Point's CREATE-side attribution is NOT implemented (a real, documented gap, not silently glossed over) — render/GGPlot.tsx's registerPointMarkArrays instead registers each Point node's FlatTensor array as a "known mark array" synchronously at RenderTree-to-Live-element construction time (which we DO control), giving WRITE-side-only corroboration (device.queue.writeBuffer's payload ArrayBuffer identity match) as a narrower fallback — never used for create attribution, per the bead's own rule that createBuffer's descriptor-only signature makes payload corroboration structurally impossible for creates. Follow-up if Point-specific create attribution is ever needed: spike @use-gpu/plot's shape-reconciler/LayerReconciler internals (traits.mjs, workbench's LayerReconciler) to find its OWN raw-source allocation call site and bracket THAT directly instead.

INSTRUMENTATION RESULTS — split by what ran where (full detail in docs/PERF_BASELINE.md):
  (a) Deno-level identity-proxy unit tests (packages/core/tests/gpu_instrument_test.ts, 9 tests) — RAN, all passing. Exercises the counting/bracket/corroboration logic against a fake GPUDevice (no real WebGPU in deno).
  (b) Real in-browser run (apps/site/scripts/gpu_instrument_check.ts driving apps/site/src/InstrumentProbe.tsx at /?instrument, via headless Chromium + --enable-unsafe-webgpu, the SAME environment apps/site's existing test:visual already proves has working headless WebGPU) — RAN, both acceptance scenarios PASS: (i) 5 re-renders of an unchanged spec -> {markBufferCreations:0, markBufferWrites:0, totalBufferCreations:5, totalBufferWrites:85}; (ii) one linear x-domain change (tzc.7) -> {markBufferCreations:0, markBufferWrites:0, totalBufferCreations:2, totalBufferWrites:18} — nonzero totals confirm the frame genuinely redraws (uniform/view writes happen and are correctly uncounted), zero mark numbers confirm no mark-data re-upload.
  Debugging footnote: the FIRST attempt at (b) showed 5 spurious mark writes on scenario (ii); root-caused to the PROBE (not the compiler) re-ingesting its raw data object on every spec rebuild, defeating PackCache's column-identity-rooted cache — fixed by pre-ingesting once, matching every other PackCache test's existing discipline. Documented as a residency-matrix gotcha for gggplot-1a6 in docs/RESIDENCY_MATRIX.md.
close_reason: Perf/conformance gate complete. Staged bench (packing/polar-transform/rendertree/emission × point/grouped-line/stacked-bar × 10k/100k/1M, 1M bounded, all 12 stages within budget). Source-boundary GPU instrumentation (gpu_instrument.ts): raw-source entry points useRawSource/useRawTensorSource→makeDataBuffer/uploadBuffer→createBuffer/writeBuffer; verified at deno level (fake device) AND real headless-Chromium WebGPU — {markBufferCreations:0, markBufferWrites:0} on both re-render and linear-domain change vs nonzero totals. 38 new conformance tests (node-budget, nested-array/owners tripwire, instrument) in default run. PERF_BASELINE.md + RESIDENCY_MATRIX.md written. Point uses write-only corroboration (delegates to plot Point — documented). Full check clean, 304 core + 5 site, fixtures --check clean, test:visual green. Honest epic verdict: 5/6 bullets pass, bullet 1 fails narrowly (boxplot whisker + label box nested → gggplot-cct). Verified by orchestrator.

description:
