title: Add GPU-native stat_count resident bars (categorical geom_bar)
description:
## Context

The only end-to-end GPU-resident product today is the unweighted 1D histogram (stat_bin → bar topology). The cheapest next product is **stat_count → resident bars** (ggplot's `geom_bar()` default on a discrete x): structurally identical to the histogram — a grouped integer reduction feeding the same bar topology — and the pieces mostly exist:

- CPU reference: `groupedCount1d` in `packages/reductions/src/cpu.ts` (valueIds × groupIds → counts matrix). Result type currently says `backend: "cpu"` only.
- WGSL patterns: `packages/reductions/src/wgsl.ts` + `gpu.ts` already implement atomic-add histogram kernels (1D and 2D) with clear/dispatch/readback plumbing and timing; a count kernel is the same shape minus the binning math (bin index = valueId directly).
- Resident runtime scaffolding: `packages/reductions/src/gpu/resident_histogram.ts`, `resident_domain.ts`; core runtime components `runtime/resident_bar.tsx` (bar topology from a count grid), `resident_live.tsx`, `resident_view.tsx`.
- Bar topology plan: `createHistogramBarTopologyPlan` in `packages/core/src/geom/bar_grid.ts` (post-refactor: in `geom/bar.ts`) already declares the grid→bars adapter with position identity/stack/dodge/fill.
- Factor columns carry levels structurally (`TypedDataFrame`), so valueIds for a discrete x are the factor codes — no CPU string hashing pass needed at render time.

Depends on the resident-capability generalization bead (per-geom `residentPlan` hooks + generic ResidentProduct node); building this on the old hardcoded path would double the special-casing.

## Scope

Eligibility gates for v1 (mirror histogram conservatism):
- `layer.geom === "bar"`, `layer.stat === "count"`, position ∈ identity/stack/dodge/fill
- cartesian, unfaceted, unweighted (`weight` param absent — weighted counts stay CPU per the floating-count policy in `stat/shared.ts`)
- x mapped to a **factor** column; no y/color/fill mapping; optional factor `group` mapping
- explicit or bounded y domain OR standalone autoYDomain via the bounded-summary path, same as histogram

Everything outside the gates falls back to the CPU `statCount` path silently.

## Steps

1. **reductions**: add a WGSL grouped-count kernel (or parameterize the existing histogram kernel: counts[groupId * valuesCount + valueId] atomic add). Extend `GroupedCount1DResult.backend` to `"cpu" | "webgpu"`. Add a GPU executor mirroring `groupedHistogram1d`'s structure in `gpu.ts`, and a resident variant in `src/gpu/` (follow `resident_histogram.ts`: keep counts in a storage buffer, expose bounded summaries — max stacked total — for y-domain metadata instead of full readback).
2. **conformance**: extend `packages/reductions/tests/gpu_test.ts` and `reductions_test.ts`: GPU results must exactly equal `groupedCount1d` CPU reference for: single group, multi-group, empty groups, 1 category, many categories (>256 to cross workgroup boundaries), and adversarial valueIds ordering. Add a benchmark entry in `bench/`.
3. **plan**: add `createStatCountProductPlan` (mirror `createStatBinProductPlan` in `stat/bin_plan.ts`) with declared inputs/outputs/dtype/dimensions; register id `@gggplot/core:stat_count@1`. Bar topology reuses the existing bar-grid plan with a `stat_count` dependency.
4. **core runtime**: a `ResidentCountProvider` (mirror `resident_live.tsx`) feeding `ResidentHistogramBars`/`resident_bar.tsx` — bar centers come from factor level index (band positions: level i at i, width 0.9) rather than bin centers. Categorical axis ticks come from the factor levels already on the CPU (levels are metadata, not data — no readback needed).
5. **eligibility**: implement `residentPlan` on the bar geom for the stat_count case alongside the existing stat_bin case, returning a `ResidentProductProps` with `product: "@gggplot/core:stat_count@1"`.
6. **docs/example**: add or extend a docs example demonstrating a large-N categorical bar chart with `resident: true`, and note count-bar residency in the Internals page's resident section.

## Constraints

- Deterministic: counts are u32 atomic adds — bit-exact vs CPU; assert exact equality, not tolerance.
- No CPU materialization of per-row stat output on the resident path; only bounded metadata (per-category stacked max, category count) crosses back for scales/guides.
- Keep the weighted path CPU-only; do not widen `statWeights` semantics.

## Verification

- All reductions tests incl. new GPU conformance cases; `resident_conformance_test.ts` extended with a count case.
- Visual: side-by-side CPU vs resident rendering of the same spec is pixel-identical (or within the established visual-baseline tolerance) for identity/stack/dodge/fill.
- Fallback: a spec with mapped fill or weight renders via CPU path unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: WGSL grouped-count kernel with GPU executor and resident variant lands in packages/reductions; GroupedCount1DResult supports backend webgpu; GPU counts are bit-exact vs groupedCount1d CPU reference across single/multi/empty-group and >256-category cases; @gggplot/core:stat_count@1 ProductPlan registered and consumed by the bar-grid topology; bar geom's residentPlan gates stat_count per the v1 eligibility list with silent CPU fallback outside gates; no per-row readback on the resident path (bounded metadata only); resident vs CPU rendering matches for identity/stack/dodge/fill; docs example added; all reductions and conformance tests pass.

If a commit referencing gggplot-2xp exists on refactor/geom-registry after c2622c4, it is UNVERIFIED — run the verification checklist in gggplot-wu0 before closing. If no commit, restart from this bead's spec; no partial work should be trusted uncommitted.

title: Move per-geom domain widening out of compile() into geom domainContribution hooks
description:
## Context

`compile()` in `packages/core/src/compile/mod.ts` hardcodes per-geom domain-widening special cases in its orchestration loop (lines ~100–148 pre-refactor):

- `widenForStackedBars(...)` called for every layer (bar stacking widens y),
- an inline silhouette-area block (`layer.geom === "area" && position === "stack" && params.offset === "silhouette"`) that recomputes per-x totals to symmetrize the y domain,
- bar/col width widening via `resolutionOf(xScale, scaledX) * 0.9` + `widenForTileAxis`,
- tile width/height widening via `widenForTileAxis` on both axes.

The bar case is then **duplicated** inside `buildPanel` for facet free-scale mode. This is geom knowledge leaked into the orchestrator — ggplot2 keeps it in each geom (setup_data / range contribution). Every new extent-bearing geom currently means editing compile() in two places.

Depends on the per-geom registry refactor (GeomDefinition in `packages/core/src/geom/types.ts`); do not start before it lands.

## Design

Add an optional hook to `GeomDefinition`:

```ts
domainContribution?(
  layer: Layer,
  mapping: Aes,
  data: DataFrame,
  ctx: {
    xScale?: TrainedScale; yScale?: TrainedScale;
    xDomain: [number, number]; yDomain: [number, number];
  },
): { x?: [number, number]; y?: [number, number] } | undefined;
```

Contract: the hook returns *replacement* domains (already merged with the incoming ctx domains, i.e. monotonically widening — a returned domain must contain the input domain). compile() loops layers generically:

```ts
for (const { layer, data, mapping } of perLayer) {
  const contrib = GEOM_REGISTRY[layer.geom].domainContribution?.(layer, mapping, data, ctx);
  if (contrib?.x) xDomain = contrib.x;
  if (contrib?.y) yDomain = contrib.y;
}
```

## Steps

1. Move the four widening behaviors into `domainContribution` on their owning geoms:
   - `bar`/`col` (bar.ts): stacked-bar y widening (`widenForStackedBars` covers geom bar/col with stack/fill positions — read its current implementation in `compile/coordinates.ts`) + x band widening (`resolutionOf * 0.9` + `widenForTileAxis`).
   - `area` (area.ts): stacked-area y widening (widenForStackedBars also handles area? verify) + the silhouette symmetric-y block moved verbatim.
   - `tile` (tile.ts): x and y widening honoring `params.width`/`params.height` overrides.
2. Keep `widenForStackedBars`/`widenForTileAxis` as helpers — either exported from `compile/coordinates.ts` as today or moved to `geom/shared.ts`; geoms import them.
3. Replace both call sites in compile(): the top-level loop over `allPerLayer` AND the per-panel loop inside `buildPanel` (free-scale mode) with the single generic loop. The per-panel loop currently only re-applies the bar cases; after this change every geom's contribution applies per panel automatically — confirm this matches current behavior for fixed scales (it should be a no-op difference) and improves free-scale correctness for tile/area (note any intentional behavior delta in the PR description).
4. Grep compile/mod.ts afterward for any remaining `layer.geom ===` comparisons; the orchestrator should have none related to domains.

## Constraints

- For `scales: "fixed"` (the default), compiled RenderTree output must be byte-identical to before for all existing fixtures/examples.
- For free scales, tile/silhouette contributions now apply per panel; if that changes any docs example rendering, document it and update visual baselines deliberately.

## Verification

- Full `deno test`; the plan/facet/pipeline tests in `packages/core/tests/` (facet_layout_test.ts, pipeline_test.ts, plan_test.ts) must pass.
- Visual smoke on apps/site, paying attention to: stacked bar chart, silhouette/streamgraph area example, tile heatmap, faceted examples with free scales if any exist.
acceptance_criteria: compile/mod.ts contains no geom-specific domain-widening branches (no layer.geom comparisons for domains, top-level or in buildPanel); bar/col, area (incl. silhouette), and tile implement domainContribution on their GeomDefinitions; contributions apply uniformly per panel including free-scale mode; fixed-scale RenderTree output is identical to before; any free-scale behavior delta is documented with updated visual baselines; full test suite and visual smoke pass.

title: Generalize resident eligibility into per-geom capability declarations and a generic ResidentProduct node
description:
## Context

GPU-resident lowering is currently a single hardcoded special case:

- `packages/core/src/compile/resident.ts` → `residentHistogramProps()` is one long conjunction gating exactly one geom×stat pair (bar+bin, cartesian, unfaceted, unweighted, no y/color/fill mapping, numeric x, optional factor group, position ∈ identity/stack/dodge/fill).
- `compile()` in `compile/mod.ts` calls it by name inside the panel-layer loop, and again special-cases `standaloneResident?.autoYDomain` for the single-layer standalone view.
- The RenderTree has product-specific `ComponentName` variants: `"ResidentHistogram"` and `"ResidentHistogramView"` (`compile/rendertree.ts`), consumed by name in the live runtime.

Adding the next resident product (e.g. stat_count bars — see follow-up bead) this way means another bespoke props function, more compile() branches, and two more ComponentName variants. This issue generalizes the mechanism so new resident products are registered, not hand-wired.

Depends on the per-geom registry refactor (GeomDefinition / GEOM_REGISTRY); do not start before it lands.

## Design

1. **Per-geom capability hook.** Add to `GeomDefinition`:

```ts
residentPlan?(
  spec: GGSpec,
  layer: Layer,
  mapping: Aes,
  data: TypedDataFrame,
  opts: { standalone: boolean },   // !faceted && single layer — enables autoYDomain
): ResidentProductProps | undefined;
```

where `ResidentProductProps` is a discriminated union:

```ts
interface ResidentProductProps {
  product: string;                  // plan id, e.g. "@gggplot/core:stat_bin@1"
  props: Record<string, unknown>;   // serializable node props (today's ResidentHistogramNodeProps)
  standaloneView?: boolean;         // today's autoYDomain standalone path
}
```

2. **Generic RenderTree node.** Replace `"ResidentHistogram"` / `"ResidentHistogramView"` with a single `"ResidentProduct"` ComponentName carrying `{ product, ...props }` (and a `view: true` prop for the standalone form). The live backend resolves `product` → component through a runtime registry (a `Record<string, LiveComponent>` in `packages/core/src/runtime/`, seeded with the histogram components from `resident_view.tsx` / `resident_mark.tsx`). The existing plan/extension registry (`packages/core/src/plan/registry.ts`, live adapters) is the natural resolver if it fits without contortion — use it if the live adapter shape works, otherwise a simple runtime map is acceptable; document the choice.

3. **compile() becomes generic.** The panel-layer loop asks `GEOM_REGISTRY[layer.geom].residentPlan?.(...)` when `options.resident` is set; the standalone-view branch keys off `standaloneView` rather than histogram-specific fields.

4. Move the histogram eligibility conjunction from `compile/resident.ts` into `geom/bar.ts`'s `residentPlan` implementation (content unchanged). `compile/resident.ts` shrinks to shared types/helpers or disappears.

## Constraints

- Behavior-preserving for the existing histogram path: same eligibility decisions, same rendered output, including the autoDomain and autoYDomain flows and CPU fallback when gates fail.
- `emitSource` must keep its current behavior for resident nodes (resident is runtime-only; emission keeps portable CPU nodes — verify `emit/mod.ts` handles/never sees ResidentProduct and preserve that).
- RenderTree stays fully serializable — the `product` id is a string, never a function/component reference.

## Verification

- `packages/core/tests/resident_conformance_test.ts` and `runtime_test.ts` pass unchanged (update only component-name assertions if they reference "ResidentHistogram" literally).
- Manual/visual check in apps/site: the resident histogram example renders identically with `resident: true`, and still falls back to CPU when a gate fails (e.g. mapped fill).
- Grep: no remaining `"ResidentHistogram"` ComponentName strings outside the runtime registry seed.
acceptance_criteria: residentHistogramProps's eligibility logic lives in the bar geom's residentPlan hook; compile() requests resident lowering generically via GEOM_REGISTRY with no product-specific branches; RenderTree uses a single serializable ResidentProduct ComponentName resolved by a runtime registry (ResidentHistogram/ResidentHistogramView variants removed); histogram eligibility decisions, rendering, autoDomain/autoYDomain flows, and CPU fallback are behavior-identical; emitSource behavior for resident specs unchanged; resident conformance and runtime tests pass.

title: WASM glyph module fails to load under Vite 8/Rolldown (blocks live WebGPU render)
description: apps/site's live WebGPU canvas renders nothing: @use-gpu/plot's Plot component always wraps children in SDFFontProvider, which requires FontContext (supplied via @use-gpu/workbench's FontLoader/FontProvider). FontProvider constructs a RustText instance backed by @use-gpu/glyph's wasm-bindgen module (pkg/use_gpu_text.js, importing use_gpu_text_bg.wasm as an ESM wasm module). That import never gets bundled: the built JS (both deno task dev and deno task build output) contains zero references to '.wasm' or 'WebAssembly', so UseRustText.new() throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading userusttext_new)'. vite-plugin-wasm (3.6.0) is configured in apps/site/vite.config.ts and claims Vite 8 support, but Vite 8.0.16 ships Rolldown (not Rollup) as its bundler by default, and the plugin's transform appears not to reach this import under Rolldown. Tried adding vite-plugin-top-level-await (+ esbuild, which the plugin needs but isn't installed) — built fine but did not fix the missing wasm reference, so reverted both.
design: Ground-truthed via Playwright: navigated to both the deno task dev server and the deno task build + preview output, same TypeError in both. grep -c 'WebAssembly|instantiate' on the built bundle returns 0, and grep for '.wasm' also returns nothing — confirms the wasm import is dropped entirely rather than a timing/async race.
acceptance_criteria: apps/site's live WebGPU panel renders the scatter+line demo with no console errors, screenshot shows visible points/line/grid (axis tick label glyphs may remain blank pending real font data — that's a separate, smaller concern).
close_reason: Root-caused and fixed via empirical testing: added a diagnostic probe plugin to vite.config.ts that logged resolveId/load calls for any '.wasm'-related module id -- it never fired once during a full build, proving Rolldown (Vite 8's default bundler, replacing Rollup) handles .wasm imports through its own native asset pipeline that bypasses the JS plugin container entirely, so vite-plugin-wasm's Rollup-style hooks never got a chance to run on @use-gpu/glyph's wasm-bindgen import. Fix: pinned apps/site's vite to ^7.3.0 (last major line with rollup as a real dependency, not rolldown) and @vitejs/plugin-react to ^5.2.0 (the only version supporting vite ^7 as well as ^8). Rebuilt: grep for WebAssembly/instantiate in the bundle now finds real instantiation glue code (previously zero matches), and the wasm file loads with 200 OK in-browser with zero console errors. Verified via Playwright screenshot -- no more 'wasm.userusttext_new' crash.

title: Generate per-geom reference docs from the geom registry
description:
## Context

The docs site (`apps/site/src/docs/`) is organized as ~14 topical pages (`pages.ts`) with 61 DocExamples, and `geom_coverage.ts` + `geom_coverage_test.ts` enforce that every public geom constructor has a live example. What's missing is a **per-geom reference index** — the ggplot2-style page a user lands on when searching "gggplot geom_boxplot": one page (or section) per geom listing its signature, default stat/position, understood aesthetics, params, GPU-residency status, and its examples. 32 of 46 geoms are only covered in `mode: "comparison"` shared examples, so several workhorse geoms (boxplot, violin, tile) have no dedicated home.

Depends on the per-geom registry refactor: `GEOM_REGISTRY` (`packages/core/src/geom/mod.ts`) becomes the machine-readable source so reference pages are generated, not hand-maintained.

## Design

1. **Enrich the registry with doc metadata.** Extend `GeomDefinition` (or a parallel `GEOM_DOCS` record in core, colocated per geom file) with serializable fields:

```ts
interface GeomDocMeta {
  /** aesthetics the lowering actually reads, required vs optional */
  aesthetics: { required: AesName[]; optional: AesName[] };
  /** recognized params with one-line descriptions, e.g. binwidth, width, coef */
  params?: Record<string, string>;
  summary: string;          // one-sentence description
  ggplot2Equivalent?: string; // e.g. "geom_histogram"
}
```

Populate from each geom's lowering code (read what `valuesOf`/`colorsOf`/params accesses it makes — do not guess; verify against the lowering source). Resident status is derived, not authored: a geom with a `residentPlan` hook reports its gate summary.

2. **Reference page(s) in the site.** Add a "Geom reference" section: either one route per geom (`/reference/geom-point`) or a single indexed page with anchors — pick whichever fits the existing `pages.ts` routing model with less machinery; per-geom routes preferred if the router supports it cheaply. Each entry renders: constructor name + DSL snippet, summary, default stat/position (from the registry — single source of truth), aesthetics table, params table, residency badge ("GPU-resident when: …" / "CPU"), and links to every DocExample listed for it in `geomExampleCoverage` (both dedicated and comparison).

3. **Extend the coverage test** (`geom_coverage_test.ts`):
   - every public geom constructor has doc metadata (aesthetics + summary non-empty);
   - every geom's reference entry links only to existing example ids (reuse the existing known-ids machinery);
   - registry defaultStat matches what the DSL constructor actually produces (compile a layer per constructor and compare — this pins the DSL↔registry single-source-of-truth invariant from the refactor).

4. **Promote thin comparison coverage** (small, bounded): give `geomBoxplot`, `geomViolin`, and `geomTile` dedicated examples if they don't have one after review (boxplot currently rides along in `LabelsAndIntervals`). Flip their `geomExampleCoverage` mode to "dedicated". Do NOT attempt dedicated examples for all 32 comparison-mode geoms — annotation/interval families are fine shared.

5. **Document annotate()'s IR-only geoms.** `segment` and `rect` are GeomKinds with full lowerings but no public constructors (reachable via `annotate()`, `AnnotateGeom` in `dsl/geoms.ts`). The coverage test intentionally can't see them. Add an explicit enumeration of accepted annotate geoms ("segment" | "rect" | "text" | "point") with a snippet each on the existing Annotations page.

## Constraints

- Doc metadata must live in core next to each geom (per-file), stay serializable, and add zero runtime weight to compile() — the site imports it, the compiler ignores it.
- Follow the existing DocExample/pages patterns (lazy data loading, synchronized DSL text + spec) described on the FAQ/contributor page.

## Verification

- `deno test` in apps/site including the extended coverage test; route-health check per the existing docs gate (see bead gggplot-1ha.1's harness).
- Visual smoke passes; new reference routes render in both the dev server and any static build.
- Spot-check 5 geoms' aesthetics tables against their lowering source for accuracy (point, bar, boxplot, text, rug).
acceptance_criteria: Every public geom constructor has serializable doc metadata (summary, required/optional aesthetics, params) colocated with its GeomDefinition; the site renders a geom reference section listing signature, defaults from the registry, aesthetics/params tables, derived GPU-residency status, and links to its coverage examples; geom_coverage_test extended to require metadata, valid example links, and DSL/registry defaultStat agreement; boxplot, violin, and tile get dedicated examples with coverage mode flipped; the Annotations page enumerates annotate()'s accepted geoms (segment/rect/text/point) with snippets; docs route-health and visual smoke pass.
notes: Unblocked (dep gggplot-elv closed @ bc4e6cc). Ready to delegate as-is: GEOM_REGISTRY and GeomDefinition live in packages/core/src/geom/{mod,types}.ts exactly as this bead assumes. Independent of gggplot-2xp; can run before or after it. See gggplot-wu0 for pipeline context and verification standards.
close_reason: Added serializable GeomDocMeta to every GEOM_REGISTRY definition and a generated geom-reference route covering all public constructors with actual alias defaults, aesthetics/params tables, derived residency, and live-example links. Added dedicated boxplot/violin examples (tile already dedicated), annotate segment/rect/text/point snippets, and strengthened coverage invariants for metadata, links, and DSL defaults. Verified deno task check, 213 core tests, 5 site tests, fixtures, production build, and geom-reference visual route.

title: Extend stat_smooth beyond linear models
description: Add deliberate loess, glm, and gam method support or explicit capability adapters.
design: Bounded V1 adds two serializable methods to existing lm: loess and glm. loess uses one-dimensional local quadratic regression with tricube weights, span default 0.75, degree fixed at 2, n default 80, and robustIterations default 2; it requires at least 3 finite distinct x values. glm supports only family binomial with logit link, fitted by deterministic IRLS with convergence/maxIterations controls and y constrained to 0/1. Both preserve effective grouping and existing se/level output; confidence bands use local weighted coefficient covariance for loess and coefficient covariance on link scale transformed through logistic for glm. gam remains explicitly unsupported in core V1: document the extension-registry adapter contract and create a separate implementation bead only if a concrete backend is selected.
acceptance_criteria: Golden numeric fixtures cover lm unchanged, loess curvature/span/grouping, logistic probabilities and convergence, se false, configurable level, insufficient/invalid inputs, and deterministic failure messages. Specs contain only serializable method/family/link parameters. CPU stat, Live tree, emitted source, facets, and gallery examples pass. Documentation explicitly lists supported formulas and the gam capability boundary.
notes: Parity references: https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/geom_smooth.html and its linked ggplot2 source. Keep method selection explicit in V1; do not copy ggplot2 automatic method switching until both data-size branches exist.
close_reason: Added explicit lm/loess/binomial-logit GLM smoothing with deterministic fitting, configurable bands, validation, GAM extension boundary docs, and live examples; 236 tests/build pass.

title: Render geom_label backgrounds
description: Complete geom_label with padded background boxes, borders, and legend behavior rather than text-only aliasing.
design: geomLabel remains text-position semantics plus a background primitive measured from the same resolved font resources used by labels. Each row produces a rounded rectangle behind its glyph run, padded by labelPadding default 3 CSS pixels and corner radius labelR default 2; fill default white, border color defaults to text color, border width default 1, alpha applies compositionally. Rotation is around the shared text/box center and box bounds are computed before rotation. z ordering is box, border, then text; label batches must retain row alignment after missing-value drops and font-face grouping. V1 does not implement collision avoidance, repel, rich text, or per-corner radii.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic measurement tests verify padding, multiline bounds, font family/face/size, rotation at 0/45/90 degrees, mapped/fixed fill and border aesthetics, missing labels, and non-overlapping buffer alignment. Render tree z order, scale/legend behavior, exact-size PNG export, Live/emitted parity, and visual fixtures on light/dark backgrounds pass. Text-only geomText output remains unchanged.
close_reason: Implemented measured rounded geomLabel boxes, borders, rotation, mapped styling, missing-row/font batch alignment, z order, emitted parity, and light/dark docs; 238 tests/build pass.

title: Add interval geom family
description: Implement crossbar, horizontal error bars, linerange, and pointrange using shared interval primitives.
design: Introduce one interval normalizer and one segment/box primitive. Vertical orientation requires x plus ymin/ymax; horizontal requires y plus xmin/xmax. orientation may be x or y and otherwise infers only when one complete mapping set is unambiguous; ambiguous or incomplete mappings error. linerange draws the stem only; pointrange adds the mapped y or x point; errorbar adds caps of width default 0.5 data-resolution units; crossbar requires the middle y or x and draws an unfilled box spanning width plus a middle line. geomErrorbarh is a deprecated-compatible alias for geomErrorbar with orientation y. Color, alpha, linetype, linewidth, and pointrange size use existing scales. V1 supports identity and existing dodge positions but does not implement middle/box-specific aesthetic overrides.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover both orientations, inference and ambiguity errors, domains including interval endpoints, cap/box widths, pointrange point placement, grouping/dodge stability, coord flip, facets, missing values, and mapped legends. DSL/IR, shared lowering topology, Live/emitted parity, and one gallery panel containing every interval form pass. Alias behavior is exact and documented.
close_reason: Implemented orientation-aware linerange, pointrange, crossbar, and horizontal errorbar alias with shared topology/validation, endpoint training, emission, and gallery docs; 228 tests/build pass.

title: Add quantile geom and stat
description: Implement grouped quantile regression lines with an explicit initial method contract.
design: V1 supports deterministic linear quantile regression for formula y~x only, separately per effective group. params.quantiles is a non-empty sorted array strictly inside (0,1), default [0.25,0.5,0.75]. params.method is rq only; unknown methods error. Fit intercept and slope by minimizing pinball loss with a deterministic solver and fixed convergence/tolerance controls, then emit two endpoint rows per quantile spanning each group x range with columns x, y, quantile, and preserved group columns. Degenerate x emits a horizontal line at the sample quantile. No splines, polynomial formulas, weights, or confidence intervals in V1.
acceptance_criteria: Reference fixtures compare intercept/slope and pinball loss to known solutions within documented tolerance for median, asymmetric quantiles, grouped data, exact-fit data, ties, and degenerate x. Invalid quantiles and insufficient finite rows fail clearly. geomQuantile defaults to line plus stat quantile. DSL/stat output, color grouping by quantile, scales, Live/emitted parity, and a gallery fixture pass.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic grouped linear quantile regression with V1 validation, quantile grouping/color scales, degenerate handling, Live/emitted rendering, and docs; 230 tests/build pass.

title: Add two-dimensional density geoms and stats
description: Implement density_2d and density_2d_filled statistical contours.
design: V1 implements grouped Gaussian product-kernel KDE on an n by n rectangular grid, default n=100. Required mappings are numeric x and y. params.h accepts a positive pair; otherwise each axis uses a deterministic normal-reference bandwidth. params.adjust accepts a positive pair default [1,1]. Output columns are x, y, density, ndensity, count=density times finite group row count, and n. Line mode feeds the existing contour stat using contourVar density, ndensity, or count; filled mode feeds contourFilled. Default breaks use 10 contour bands; explicit breaks/bins/binwidth reuse current contour precedence. Non-finite rows drop before grouping. V1 always contours and excludes arbitrary downstream geom selection.
acceptance_criteria: Numeric fixtures verify density normalization approximately integrates to one, bandwidth/adjust/grid effects, group isolation, ndensity maximum one, count relation, missing-row handling, contour variable selection, and shared facet breaks. DSL constructors, stats, contour lowering, Live/emitted parity, legends, and line/filled gallery fixtures pass. Invalid bandwidth, grid, and contourVar values throw actionable errors.
close_reason: Implemented grouped 2D Gaussian KDE line/filled stats and geoms with computed density columns, bandwidth controls, contour variables, validation, Live/emitted rendering, and docs; 226 tests/build pass.

title: Add geom_count and stat_sum
description: Implement ggplot2-compatible count-sized point rendering and stat_sum aggregation.
design: stat sum groups by the complete effective tuple of x, y, and inferred discrete grouping aesthetics. It emits one row per tuple with computed n and prop; n is row count or the finite weight sum when params.weight names a numeric column or is a finite scalar. prop is n divided by the panel total within the effective group. geomCount is geomPoint with stat sum and default size mapped to n using area semantics: rendered radius is proportional to sqrt(n), with a visible minimum for positive counts. V1 does not add delayed after_stat syntax; the constructor installs the computed size mapping directly, while explicit user size wins.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover duplicate x/y pairs, weighted fractional n, non-finite weights, effective color/fill grouping, panel-local proportions, explicit size override, facets, and zero/one-row inputs. DSL, stat output, trained size scale, Live render tree, emitted source, legend, and gallery fixture agree. Computed columns are named n and prop and remain serializable.
close_reason: Implemented stat_sum and geomCount with weighted tuple aggregation, group/panel-local proportions, area-scaled size/legend semantics, facets, emitted source, and docs; 224 tests and build pass.

title: Add missing simple geom constructors and aliases
description: Implement and test geom_freqpoly, geom_blank, geom_step, geom_curve, geom_spoke, geom_rug, and explicit geom_function/geom_jitter sugar where useful.
design: V1 contracts: geomFreqpoly is geomLine plus stat bin, sorted bin centers, y=count unless supplied, grouping preserved; geomBlank trains mapped scales and facets but emits no marks or legend keys; geomStep lowers sorted x/y into explicit vertices with direction hv default and supports vh and mid; geomCurve requires x/y/xend/yend and lowers a deterministic 32-segment quadratic approximation with curvature default 0.5; geomSpoke requires x/y/angle/radius and derives xend/yend; geomRug emits clipped panel-edge ticks with sides default bl and length in CSS pixels; geomFunction is public sugar for line plus stat function; geomJitter is point plus position jitter. No arrowheads, outside-panel rug annotations, or adaptive curve tessellation in V1.
acceptance_criteria: Every named constructor is exported through the stable DSL barrel and has exact IR defaults. Unit tests cover required mappings, grouping, missing values, step direction, curve/spoke endpoints, rug sides, blank scale training, and alias equivalence. Render-tree snapshots prove no blank marks and expected topology. Live and emitted source produce equivalent nodes. Gallery fixtures cover freqpoly, step/curve/spoke/rug, and aliases. Unsupported parameters fail clearly rather than silently changing semantics.
close_reason: Implemented all eight simple geom constructors/aliases with validated lowering, topology tests, emitted-source coverage, and live gallery documentation; 222 tests and production build pass.

title: Add physical units, DPI, and scale compatibility to plot export
description: Extend the proven pixel-sized PNG export API with ggsave-like width/height units (in, cm, mm, px), DPI, and scale. Define the conversion formula and safety limits without introducing R's implicit device or last-plot state.
design: Use one conversion pipeline: physical size -> base pixels via DPI -> output pixels via scale, while separately deciding whether layout occurs at base or output resolution to preserve typography proportions. Do not add vector formats in this bead.
acceptance_criteria: Documented conversion produces exact output pixels for in/cm/mm/px at chosen DPI and scale; rounding policy and maximum-size guard are deterministic; CSS layout size versus output resolution is explicitly defined; tests cover unit conversions, scale, rounding, and limits; pixel-only callers retain unchanged behavior.
notes: Extended ggsave with units px/in/cm/mm, dpi (default 300), and scale (default 1). resolveExportSize uses physical inches*dpi*scale with one final round-half-up; Canvas pixelRatio=scale and layout=output/scale preserves typography proportions. Pixel callers remain unchanged. Deterministic validation covers positive size/DPI/scale and adapter max dimension after conversion. Docs updated. Tests cover all units, rounding, scale, and unchanged px; browser exported 2in x 1in at 100 DPI scale 2 as exact 400x200 PNG with no live-canvas mutation/leak. 203 tests and check/build pass.
close_reason: Physical units, DPI, scale, layout-resolution policy, tests, docs, and browser proof complete.

title: Prototype WGPU stat_bin histogram kernel spike
description: Follow-up from gggplot-619 / docs/WGPU_STATS_RESEARCH.md. Prototype the narrowest credible GPU stat path: numeric stat_bin counts over Float32Array x with optional Uint32Array effective group ids, producing a Uint32Array counts matrix [nGroups, nBins]. This should stay behind the existing stat API and typed DataFrame/buffer-lowering boundary; it is a spike to measure correctness and upload/dispatch/readback cost, not a replacement for the CPU implementation. Suggested shape: CPU reference from current statBin, upload x/groupId via UseGPU raw storage sources, zero a counts buffer, dispatch one WGSL invocation per row using atomicAdd into counts[group*nBins+bin], read back counts, and expand them back into post-stat DataFrame rows. Compare small (<1k), medium (mpg/txhousing), and large (diamonds ~54k) row counts once datasets exist.
acceptance_criteria: A prototype branch or scratch implementation demonstrates the grouped histogram kernel end-to-end or documents the exact blocker. Results compare correctness and rough timings against CPU statBin, including upload/readback overhead. No public API change unless a later design bead approves it.
close_reason: Implemented groupedHistogram1dGpu in packages/reductions with WGSL atomic binning, readback, parity tests, GPU benchmark command, and docs/WGPU_STAT_BIN_SPIKE.md recording the local no-adapter timing blocker.

title: Research WGPU/WGSL shader path for statistical reductions and grouped stats
description: Investigate whether gggplot stats can eventually use WGPU/WGSL compute shaders for high-row-count operations without changing the core CPU-side grammar abstraction. Current finding: UseGPU exposes promising low-level compute, tensor/grid, readback, and contour primitives, but no ready group-by/count/bin/summary engine. The WGPU path should be treated as a future optimization target behind the typed DataFrame / buffer-lowering boundary, not the primary stat API. Research questions: can count/bin/summary/density be expressed as reusable compute kernels over lowered typed buffers; what reduction and prefix-sum patterns are required for group-by-style aggregation; whether existing UseGPU compute/readback primitives are enough; whether WGSL shader snippets already shipped in UseGPU can be reused for reductions or buffer manipulation; and whether external GPU compute projects such as tracel-ai/cubecl (https://github.com/tracel-ai/cubecl) and tracel-ai/cubek (https://github.com/tracel-ai/cubek) offer reusable ideas, algorithms, or constraints for reductions on WebGPU. Output should identify the lowest-risk first prototype, likely histogram/bin count over a numeric column with optional factor-coded group ids, and explicitly compare JS CPU implementation complexity/performance against a GPU path including upload/readback overhead.
acceptance_criteria: A research note or docs update summarizes UseGPU compute/readback primitives relevant to stats, WGSL reduction/group-by patterns needed for count/bin/summary/density, findings from cubecl/cubek, and a recommended first prototype scope. Follow-up implementation beads are created only if the research identifies a credible prototype with clear payoff.
close_reason: Completed WGPU/WGSL stats research in docs/WGPU_STATS_RESEARCH.md and filed prototype follow-up gggplot-vmv.

title: Add facet free scales (scales="free"/"free_x"/"free_y")
description: docs/COVERAGE_BACKLOG.md section 7. facet_wrap/facet_grid currently always share one fixed x/y domain across every panel (compile()'s scale training runs once over all panels combined). ggplot2's default is shared/fixed scales too, but scales='free'/'free_x'/'free_y' let each panel train its own domain independently -- useful when panels cover very different y ranges. Needs per-panel scale training instead of the current single global trainScales() call, threaded through to each panel's Cartesian/Polar range.

Keep current facet paths as CPU fallback until per-panel source handles, caching keys, and invalidation policy are specified and tested.

For resident grids, dodge2/jitterdodge/nudge must be a GPU compute or uniform transform with declared shape and direct mark consumption; do not expose a GPU mode until CPU conformance, zero-cell behavior, and no-readback execution are proven. CPU positions remain explicit fallback.

Both should compose with the Coord.project field added in gggplot-1be.3 rather than reintroducing a special case.

Extend the declarative Coord contract and preserve GPU product handles across view changes; retain CPU fallback only for marks/projections not yet represented by a GPU consumer.

This should reduce awkward inheritAes:false use for annotations and provide a clear home for non-data guide-like marks.

title: Generalize coordinate projection beyond coordFlip

Evaluate replacing coordFlip's special-case axes swizzle with a more general projection model in IR/compile that can support cartesian swaps, polar angle/radius naming, and future coordinate systems while preserving current coordFlip ergonomics.

Removed the dead unreachable 'fixed' CoordKind. Tests: 1 new case (coord_polar theta:'y'), full suite 81/81 passing. This closes epic gggplot-1be (9/9 children complete).

title: Separate simultaneous color and fill scales in compiler
description: compile() collapses color/fill to a single colorScale via scales.get('color') ?? scales.get('fill'). That works when only one aesthetic is mapped, but plots with both color and fill mappings can apply the color scale to fill-based geoms/legends. Keep separate colorScale and fillScale paths through lowerLayer/lowerBarLayer/lowerTileLayer/legends, with tests covering a point color layer plus a filled bar/tile layer.
design: Kept color and fill as independent trained scales in compile(): colorScale=scales.get('color'), fillScale=scales.get('fill'). title: Subdivide (munch) Polygon/Grid edges for clean coord_polar wedges
description: coord_polar's infrastructure is wired up and works for point geoms (verified visually), but bar/polygon-based geoms (geom_bar/col/area/ribbon/tile/boxplot) render as distorted fans instead of clean pie/rose wedges, because Polygon's straight 2-point edges don't curve under Polar's nonlinear vertex shader transform (getPolarPosition) -- only the endpoints bend, leaving long straight chords. Real ggplot2 solves this with coord_munch(), which subdivides straight path segments into many small steps before a non-linear coordinate transform, so each tiny segment approximates a smooth curve. The Grid guide has the same issue (fans out instead of showing concentric rings + radial spokes) -- worth checking whether @use-gpu/plot's Grid component has its own polar-aware config, or whether it needs a different guide entirely under Polar.

title: stat_smooth (lm/loess)
description: Fit trend + optional CI ribbon. Backs geom_smooth.
close_reason: Implemented stat_smooth with method='lm' (ordinary least-squares linear regression) in packages/core/src/stat/mod.ts. Re-emits x as params.n (default 80) evenly spaced points across the data's x range (bin-center style, like stat_bin), with fitted y, and unless params.se===false, ymin/ymax for a CI ribbon -- mapping.y/ymin/ymax always overridden to the new column names since the fitted point count differs from the input row count. CI band uses the standard OLS prediction formula se(y_hat) = s*sqrt(1/n + (x-xbar)^2/Sxx) but a fixed z=1.96 multiplier rather than the exact Student's-t critical value (large-sample approximation, documented in a code comment as a known simplification -- not a full stats package). loess (ggplot2's default method) is NOT implemented -- it's a substantially bigger lift (weighted local regression with a bandwidth/span parameter); an unrecognized method value warns and falls back to lm. Added geomSmooth() to the DSL (packages/core/src/dsl/mod.ts) and a 'smooth' GeomKind (ir/types.ts). Wired rendering in compile/mod.ts: geom_smooth lowers to an optional Ribbon Polygon (drawn first, light-indigo #c7d2fe fill, only when ymin/ymax are mapped) plus a Line for the fit -- reuses the existing bandPositions/positionsOf helpers. y-domain widening for the ribbon comes for free since trainScales already unions mapping.y/ymin/ymax for the y aesthetic. Tested with exact-value assertions: stat_smooth against noise-free linear data (y=2x+1, zero residual -> deterministic fitted values and a zero-width CI band, verifying the regression math exactly), se:false omitting ymin/ymax, and full compile() tests checking the Line+Polygon RenderNode shapes and that se:false skips the Polygon entirely. 4 new tests, all passing.
